items.title: The exported document strips the excerpt and the calculation inputs, so the platform's one decisive advantage is invisible and slower to use than a URL
items.problem: This is the most surprising result in the record and the one the platform should have won outright: 259 of 259 citations verified, 3,335 calculation rows replayed with zero divergence, every artefact hashed — and the platform won verifiability in none of the nine comparisons (console in six, equal in three). Worse, checking was measurably slower: minutes to check three figures, platform 10–30, console 10–15. Every judge described the same two obstacles. First, a fact footnote resolves to a whole document: msft1's [^1]–[^4], [^12]–[^15], [^26], [^63] and [^72] are byte-identical lines pointing at `companyfacts/CIK0000789019.json` with no XBRL concept, period or value, so — msft1 reader — "$331,839m cannot be located", and azn2 sceptic calls it "a multi-megabyte JSON of every tagged fact across all years … with no way to confirm which tag was used". Narrative footnotes point at a whole 10-K or 20-F "with no item number, page or quoted excerpt". Second, a calculation footnote gives the formula, the result and a code version but never the inputs, so "a ratio can be checked only after sourcing its inputs independently" and the DCF per-share outputs "cannot be checked at all". The msft1 reader judge's summary is the finding: "A's provenance apparatus is better in kind — hashes, formulas, code versions, tiers, point-in-time — while B's is better in practice: nearly every B figure is reproducible from the tables it prints." The audit reached the same place from the other side: "The platform's verifiability advantage lives in the interface, not in the document it exports." The exhibits compound it: three charts export as a caption plus a run of bare footnote markers under "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*", which is how msft1's five-year margin series and its 25-cell sensitivity grid became unreadable footnote litter the body then contradicted.
items.rootCause: The renderer's footnote builder carries strictly less than the database holds. `_footnotes` (src/aer/render/document.py:742-800) emits a SourceFootnote of title, url, publisher, publication date, retrieval date and tier — and no excerpt and no locator, though `citations.excerpt` is stored and is the very thing `aer.verify.citations` re-reads and confirms (src/aer/verify/citations.py:1-28, 172). It emits a CalculationFootnote of formula, value, unit, function_ref, code-version prefix and period label — and no inputs, though `Calculation.inputs` is a JSONB array of each input with its unit and source (src/aer/db/models/calculation.py:76, and the module docstring at :21 says a calculation without its inputs "is not a partial record, it is an unusable one"). Exhibits export as caption plus markers by construction: src/aer/render/markdown.py:249-256.

items.recommendation: Print what is already stored. A fact footnote should carry the verified excerpt (the one code confirmed) and the locator that found it — for an XBRL fact, the concept name, the period and the unit; for a filing, the item and the quoted sentence. A calculation footnote should carry its inputs by name, value and unit, each with its own citation marker, so a ratio is re-performable on the page. An exhibit should export its underlying series as a table in the Markdown, not as a caption plus loose markers. None of this touches an invariant — it is the opposite: it makes invariants 1, 2 and 3 legible to the person the report is for. It is also the cheapest large win in this area, and it is the item that would have let the platform win verifiability outright in all nine comparisons.

items.title: The front page prints a value per share that matches neither valuation method, with no period and no method name
items.problem: All three msft1 judges nominated the same first_thing_to_check, and it was the front page. msft1 sceptic: "The 'At a glance' pair 'Value per share (base) $485.29' and 'Free cash flow $139,225m': neither is reconciled to the body — the DCF section's own outputs are $242.78 (Gordon growth) and $449.79 (exit multiple), and operating cash flow less capex from the document's own figures is ~$67bn." msft1 operator: "Until that headline is reconciled — and set against a price — nothing else in the note can be acted on." The reader judge traced $485.29 to the top of the football-field range. Both figures are traceable, footnoted and arithmetically correct; what misleads is a missing label and a missing period. The free-cash-flow half is fixed (F-11; azn2 correctly shows FY2025 $11,765m), but the value-per-share half survives: azn2's front page prints "Value per share (base) | — | $169.80" with an em-dash period and no method name, while the valuation section shows $169.80 (exit multiple) and $333.48 (Gordon) — a 96% spread the front page collapses into one unexplained number.
items.rootCause: `_HEADLINE_CALCULATIONS` (src/aer/render/glance.py:98-110) shows "the latest run of each" curated name, and `_headline` (:354-360) admits any row whose `case` parameter is absent or 'base'. Football-field endpoints and both terminal methods are recorded as `value_per_share` with no case tag, so the row that wins is whichever was written last — on msft1 that was the football-field maximum. The period column falls back to an em-dash when `period_label` is null, which it is for every valuation output, so nothing on the front page says what the figure is of or by what method. The F-11 fix addressed the same class of bug for free cash flow by renaming the DCF's projections to `forecast_free_cash_flow`; the equivalent discrimination for per-share outputs was not made.

items.title: Sections spend their budget narrating what the run could not find, including research housekeeping, and the refusal wording blames the issuer
items.problem: Two judges nominated the same runner-up for weakest paragraph, and it is a section that should be the easiest in the document. azn2 sceptic on Business Overview: "a 600-word unbroken paragraph on a company whose therapy areas, products and geographies are never named, which instead advises that 'any register search intended to trace applicant-of-record status for AstraZeneca products should therefore not be limited to the parent company name alone' — housekeeping for a different task, occupying the section that should carry the business." msft1's Industry & Competitive Positioning states "no peer figures are presented here as a result; this is a gap rather than a judgement" and names no company. Beyond the wasted budget, the refusal wording repeatedly asserts something false about the issuer: msft1's Segment Analysis says segment figures "were available" nowhere, when the console pulled them from an exhibit of the same accession; azn2 says the 20-F's notes are incorporated by reference, when the FY2025 results announcement lists product revenue line by line. The azn2 operator judge named the pattern exactly: "a retrieval limit presented as a disclosure limit". This matters for trust, not just tone — a reader who can show one 'not available' claim is false discounts the rest, and two judges said so.
items.rootCause: When a section's evidence pack is thin the writer is still given its full token budget and a contract to fill, so it fills the space with an account of the absence; the degradation machinery (ADR 0055, ADR 0099, ADR 0100) caps *gap remarks* and shortens sections but does not stop a section writing 600 words about its own research. `presentation_integrity` does count gap sentences and process language against a budget of one per section (src/aer/eval/runtime.py:297-308), and it scored zero defects on azn2, so its process-language register does not catch advice addressed to a future researcher. Separately, nothing in the section contract or the writer's instructions distinguishes 'the issuer does not disclose this' from 'this run did not retrieve it', and the writer has no way to know which is true — it sees an evidence pack, not a list of what was not fetched.

items.recommendation: Three changes, all small. (1) Scale a section's token budget to its evidence: a section that clears its policy by one thin source gets a short budget, so it says the little it can say and stops, rather than writing 600 words of method. (2) Extend the process-language register to catch advice addressed to a researcher rather than a reader ('register search', 'should not be limited to', 'any search intended to'), so `presentation_integrity` fails on it as it already does on UUIDs. (3) Distinguish the two kinds of absence in the wording by giving the writer, in its input, the list of documents the run selected and did not fetch — so 'not disclosed by the issuer' is reserved for cases the run actually checked, and everything else says 'not retrieved for this run'. That last one is honest, costs an hour, and removes the specific claim three judges caught being false.

items.title: `reports.rating` is assigned None on every run and nothing else ever writes it
items.problem: Every report the platform has ever produced says "Non-binding view: no view reached" at the top, on every surface: the Markdown, the HTML, the PDF, the one-pager, the reports list ("No conclusion produced"), the company history, the Obsidian export, and the prior-research comparison of the next run. Six of six blind judge comparisons named this as the first reason the console note was preferred (audit §4.1). It reads as an honest abstention after deliberation; it is a literal `None`.

items.recommendation: Do not let a model write this field. Two of the four options below are compliant and cheap; take them together. Compose the *figure* half deterministically (the valuation range, item `valuation-range-columns-never-filled`) and let the *label* half be the operator's own, stated at approval (item `operator-cannot-state-a-view`). Until the operator surface exists, the interim move that costs nothing and removes the worst reading is option A: stop printing a fallback that claims deliberation, and print the composed range instead. A model-written rating (option D) is the one I would refuse: a one-word label with no holder, no time and no stated basis is the closest thing this tool can produce to regulated advice, it is what `RESERVED_OUTPUT_FIELDS` exists to keep out of skill files (`src/aer/core/schemas/skill.py:64-92`), and permitting it through the built-in door while refusing it through the skill door would make invariant 7 a statement about file formats rather than about ratings.

options.change: Replace the fallback at `render/markdown.py:162` and `report.html:158`. Where a valuation exists, print the composed base-case range and the method; where none exists, print the one-line reason the value step recorded (`services/valuation_run.py` output `reason`, already rendered by `sections/valuation_method.py:110-123`). Nothing is invented and nothing is a model's.
options.cost: Half a session. Touches the byte-pinned golden fixture `tests/fixtures/full_run/golden.md:8` and `tests/test_run_api.py:1769`.
options.risk: A judge may still say no view is *stated* — a range is not a thesis. It removes the contradiction and buys no verdict on its own.

options.name: B — The operator states it at the final gate
options.change: The approval form gains a short view field and a basis. Stored as a `judgements`/`premises` row through `services/theses.py` (ADR 0102), with `theses.report_id` pointing at the report, and mirrored into `reports.rating` for display. A named person, a time, a stated basis.
options.cost: Two to three sessions with the surface. Needs a new ADR.
options.risk: Adds a step to an already six-to-seven-stop journey (audit §4.2). The operator may skip it, and a field that is usually blank is worse than none.

options.name: C — Compose it from the run's own rows
options.change: A deterministic label derived from recorded calculations alone — for example the base-case range against a market anchor, banded. Pure Python, traceable, no model.
options.cost: One session, but it depends on `no-price-anchor-for-the-per-share-figure` being settled first.
options.risk: A banded label computed from one DCF is a rating in all but name, produced by a rule nobody agreed to. It would need an ADR stating the rule, and it invites exactly the false precision the platform exists to avoid.

options.risk: Refused. It is the one thing `RESERVED_OUTPUT_FIELDS` and ADRs 0037/0040/0074 are built to prevent, it puts the model's opinion under a name a reader takes for a conclusion, and it sits closest to the advice line CLAUDE.md draws.

items.title: The section writers' evidence pack excludes every run-level valuation figure, by SQL
items.problem: The Executive Summary and the Investment Thesis — the two sections a reader goes to for the view — are drafted without ever being shown the run's WACC, terminal values, enterprise value or value per share. So they truthfully report that no valuation exists, on the same page that prints one. MSFT #1: "no valuation output, no discount rate and no peer multiple, so we take no view on whether the 11 September 2026 share price is fair" (report.md:46) and "No discounted cash flow, cost of equity, weighted average cost of capital, terminal value, value per share or peer multiple sits on this record" (report.md:51), against "WACC — 9.3%" and "Value per share (base) — $485.29" at report.md:39-40. AZN #2 does the same at report.md:53 against report.md:40. This is the single largest reason a judge cannot find an argued view: the arguing sections are starved of the only figures that could anchor one.
items.rootCause: `src/aer/sections/evidence.py:580-588` selects the calculation listing with `ORDER BY Calculation.period_end DESC NULLS LAST, Calculation.sequence` and `LIMIT EVIDENCE_ITEM_CAP` (40, defined at line 97). `src/aer/calc/engine.py:165-169` states that a calculation's period is "None for one whose result is not a statement-period figure at all (a discount rate, a price multiple)" — so every DCF output carries `period_end = NULL` and sorts behind every ratio row. MSFT #1 recorded 852 calculations (summary.json `replay.calculations_checked`); the ratio suite alone strikes far more than 40 period-stamped rows, so the NULLS-LAST tail is never reached and the valuation is excluded at the database, before the token budget is consulted. The comment at lines 572-579 shows the trade-off was seen and deliberately taken — to stop sensitivity-grid cells filling the cap — but the consequence was not: no figure survives for the writers at all. The same rows reach the front page uncapped through `src/aer/render/glance.py:328-351`, and reach the valuation section uncapped through `src/aer/sections/valuation_method.py:125-131`, which is why one document says both things.

items.title: Nothing requires the Investment Thesis to reach a view, and nothing checks it against the run's own record
items.problem: The section built to state the view is free to decline to. On MSFT #1 it wrote "we state the propositions and their tests and offer no verdict on the share price" (report.md:77); on AZN #2 it wrote "we hold a constructive but low-confidence view" (report.md:78) — and three of three judges then marked AZN #2 "view stated and argued" where three of three had marked MSFT #1 "no". The difference was the draft, not the policy. Worse, the section is free to assert the absence of figures the run holds, and did, in every run examined. A judge reading AZN #2 called the result "contradictions, and a reader cannot tell which half to believe".
items.rootCause: `investment_thesis` requires only `thesis_statement` and `supporting_pillars` as free strings (migration 0023:119-150). The section writer holds no tools and is validated only for contract shape, claim well-formedness and numeral sourcing (`src/aer/sections/evidence.py:validate_draft`, `src/aer/core/section_output.py`) — none of which can notice that a sentence denies a recorded calculation. `src/aer/sections/valuation_method.py:1-19` states the general principle for exactly this failure ("A section can evade the whole validation apparatus by being confidently qualitative") and solves it for `valuation_dcf` with a `SectionAugmenter` — a platform-filled block the model never sees, a `note` telling the writer what it may name, and a `check` that refuses a commentary naming what the record does not hold (`src/aer/sections/deterministic.py:380-411`). `investment_thesis` and `executive_summary` have no augmenter: `AUGMENTERS` contains exactly one key (`deterministic.py:404-411`).

items.recommendation: Give `investment_thesis` a `SectionAugmenter` in the ADR 0063 shape: `build` renders the view's figure block from the ledger (base case, the two terminal methods, the discount rate, the range, and — if `no-price-anchor-for-the-per-share-figure` is settled — the anchor), `note` tells the writer which figures the block carries so it argues from them, and `check` refuses a draft that asserts the absence of a component the block holds. It needs no new ADR — ADR 0063 already decided the pattern and ADR 0087's split (composed half, authored half) already decided the posture. Add `what_would_change_the_view` to `required` at the same time: a falsifier list is what turns a recited view into an argued one, and the judges read it as such on AZN #2.

A missing rating and a deliberate abstention look identical unless one of them says so" — and it is correct in isolation and wrong in this document, because the third state (a view stated in the body and not in the column) was not anticipated.

items.title: A refresh report tells its reader a view will be recorded at approval, and none ever is
items.problem: Every refresh run's Prior Research Comparison prints three rows whose "current" column reads "Recorded at this run's approval." — for the non-binding view, the confidence and the valuation range. Nothing records any of them, at approval or ever. AZN #2's own report carries the row verbatim: "| Non-binding view | no view reached | Recorded at this run's approval. |". The prior column is equally hollow: because every past report's rating is null, the comparison can only ever say the earlier run reached no view. The refresh journey — audit use case 2, the one the platform scores "yes, once fixed" on — therefore compares two blanks and promises a third.

items.title: The operator has nowhere to state their own view about the report they are approving
items.problem: The operator reads a 14,000-word note, forms a view, and approves the document — and the platform records only "approved" plus an optional free-text note. The view they formed exists nowhere, so the report they share states none, the next run cannot be framed against it, the thesis monitor has nothing new to monitor, and the reports list says "No conclusion produced". This is the user-ready half of the problem as much as the judge-facing half: a research tool whose whole point is one report at a time under human approval never asks the human what they concluded.
items.rootCause: The final gate's form offers a decision and a "Notes (optional)" textarea (`src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:101-109`) plus per-disagreement rationales (`runs/review.html:68-79`); `Approval` has columns for gate, decision, actor, notes and payload hash and nothing else (`src/aer/db/models/approval.py:33-75`). The record that *should* hold the view already exists and is complete: ADR 0102's `judgements` supertype (holder, two clocks, a NOT NULL basis, supersession, withdrawal-with-reason), `premises` as its subtype, and `theses` carrying `report_id` to the report it was written against (`src/aer/db/models/judgement.py:91-200`), with `services/theses.py` the only writer and `reports_to_write_against` already offering approved reports to the form (`services/theses.py:391-404`). What is missing is the path from a run to that form and the render back into the document. ADR 0074 explicitly permits it: "a Judgement may be displayed: a badge on a position, a column in the decision log, the basis text in full" — what it may not do is enter arithmetic or become a `SourceRef`.

items.recommendation: This is the compliant answer to "what does a view look like for a personal research tool that is not investment advice", and it is the one I would build: not a rating the platform produces, but a view the operator holds — a named person, a time, a basis that cannot be blank, premises each with either a testable predicate or a date they will look again, and a falsifier list. It is not advice because nobody is advising anybody; it is the operator's own research journal, which is what this tool is. The smallest version: after approval, the run offers "state your view" prefilled from the section the model already wrote — the thesis statement as the title, `what_would_change_the_view` as candidate premises — which the operator edits, accepts or discards, and which is stored through `services/theses.py` with the report id. The report then renders the operator's view where the header's rating is, labelled as theirs and dated. A new ADR is required for two reasons: it makes the approval gate a write of a judgement (ADR 0087 and ADR 0102 each stopped short of that deliberately), and prefilling a judgement from a model's prose puts machine text into the table meant for the operator's own, which ADR 0087 named as the thing not to do without saying so.

items.title: `reports.confidence` is an empty column whose obvious filling would launder a model's opinion into a figure
items.problem: The report row carries a `confidence` float with a probability check constraint, the renderers print it as a percentage when present (`render/markdown.py:163-164`, `report.html:159-161`), the specification's example sets it to 0.62, and it is null on every run. items.title: A page a worker fetches is hashed and stored but never excerpted, so nothing can ever cite it
items.problem: Every route by which news or secondary analysis could reach a section dead-ends here. A worker-fetched document produces a source_documents row and an artefact, and no Extraction rows. A section's evidence pack builds its excerpts only from Extraction rows; a claim's citation is an extraction id, validated against the pack and recorded as an extraction id. So a T5 page — or a T1 exhibit, once the tier is fixed — arrives in the listing as a title with no text, and no claim can stand on it. items.title: The reader is shown a tier only in a footnote, and it is the recorded tier, not the one policy used
items.problem: Nothing in the document tells a reader that a paragraph rests on secondary reporting. There is a marker for an undated source — a dagger with a one-line legend — and nothing for tier. The footnote prints a tier string, and it prints source_tier, the recorded tier, not evidence_tier, the capped one policy actually judged by: an undated EDGAR filing footnotes as 'tier T1_REGULATORY' while the shortfall check counted it as tier 5. Today that asymmetry is mostly harmless because no built-in section can cite anything looser than T4. The moment the ceiling rises it is the difference between a marked claim and an unmarked one, and it is the thing that decides whether a sceptical judge trusts the document.

items.title: Two accepted ADRs combine to switch web search off silently on any run that crosses midnight UTC
items.problem: ADR 0092 refuses web_search whenever the run is point-in-time and its as-of date is earlier than today. ADR 0110 makes the as-of date a stamp written when the run is commissioned. A run commissioned on Monday evening and still researching on Tuesday morning is therefore dated Monday, and every web search in it is refused — deterministically, correctly by each rule on its own, and invisibly to the operator, since the refusal lands in the worker's audit trail and nowhere a person looks. AZN's first run was commissioned 2026-09-11 and researched 2026-09-12; MSFT #2 and AZN #2, both same-day, did search. The one capability that closes the recency gap is switched off by the clock.
items.rootCause: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/src/aer/services/research.py:368-382 refuses when request.work_order.point_in_time and as_of_date < today. /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/docs/adr/0110 makes as_of_date a commission-time stamp and names the case explicitly: 'a run commissioned on Monday and still acquiring on Tuesday is dated Monday'. Point-in-time defaults on.
evidence: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/src/aer/services/research.py:368-382
/home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/docs/adr/0110-a-run-is-dated-by-the-platform-not-by-the-operator.md — 'The second look-ahead check keeps its job, on a smaller argument'
/home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn/summary.json — as_of_date 2026-09-11, started_at 2026-09-12T07:17Z
/home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft2/worker.log:220,223 and azn2/worker.log:232,246,250 — provider.web_search fired on the same-day runs only
Hypothesis, not measured: AZN #1's searches were refused for this reason; that run's worker log is not in the export
items.recommendation: Option B. The rule ADR 0092 is protecting is 'nothing published after the as-of date may inform this run', and a search run today against a run stamped yesterday breaks it only by a day — but the ADR's deeper point stands, that a live index cannot be bounded and a result's own date is attacker-controlled. The honest fix is to stop the situation arising: refuse the search only when the stamp is meaningfully in the past, and make the refusal visible on the run page when it happens, so an operator who has lost the capability knows. Whichever option is taken, the refusal must stop being silent.

options.name: A — leave the rule, surface the refusal
options.change: Nothing in the logic; add the refusal to the run console's step readout and the report's coverage notice.
options.risk: None. Honest, and does not recover the capability.

options.name: B — a one-day grace, plus the visible refusal
options.change: Refuse only when the stamp is more than a day old, on the argument that a run whose stamp is today or yesterday cannot admit anything materially post-dated, and that the look-ahead check at acquisition still runs on everything fetched.
options.cost: A comparison and an ADR amendment.
options.risk: It weakens a rule stated as absolute. It needs ADR 0092 amended, not a code change smuggled past it, and the grace must be a named constant with the argument beside it.

options.name: C — re-stamp a long-running run
options.change: Advance the as-of date while a run is still acquiring.
options.risk: Refuse. ADR 0110's freeze exists precisely because moving the as-of date makes evidence that was admissible inadmissible, and the approval hashes are computed against it.

options.name: D — commission and research in one sitting
options.change: A workflow rule that a run must finish acquiring the day it starts.
options.risk: Unenforceable against a gate that waits on a person, which is what makes runs cross midnight in the first place.

items.challengeNote: Add the option the set is missing, which is cleaner than option B and needs no ADR amendment: compare the stamp against the run's own commission time rather than against wall-clock today — the rule ADR 0092 states is that a live index cannot be bounded by a date in the past, and a run stamped at its own commissioning is not in the past relative to itself. That fixes the midnight case exactly, keeps the rule absolute for a genuinely back-dated run, and changes one comparison. Recommend that over option B, and keep option A's visible refusal either way. Also downgrade the item's certainty language from "switched off" to "would be switched off", or re-run the AZN brief overnight and measure it (~£7).

items.title: Inadmissible sources consume slots in the forty-row cap before the ceiling drops them
items.problem: The sources listing queries at most EVIDENCE_ITEM_CAP rows ordered newest-retrieved-first, and only then filters on the section's tier ceiling. Worker-fetched T5 documents are retrieved last in a run, so they sort to the top of that ordering and occupy slots that are then discarded — a section can be handed fewer admissible sources than the cap allows while admissible ones sit just outside it. It did not bite in the audit runs, which held roughly a dozen documents each, but it is exactly the failure mode gap A39 and gap R8 already cost this codebase twice: the ordering clause becoming the real selector.
items.rootCause: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/src/aer/sections/evidence.py:615-635 — .limit(EVIDENCE_ITEM_CAP) on the query, then the admissible list comprehension in Python.

One line still, but say which line.

items.title: A content field may name a source document the ceiling excluded from that section
items.problem: The tier ceiling controls what a section is shown; it does not control what a section's content may name. The closed-world check for ids inside content resolves source_document_id against the full tier index — every source document on the request, including the ones the ceiling dropped and the ones that are quarantined — rather than against the admissible listing. A figure row could therefore carry a source_document_id for a document the section was never dealt, and it would pass validation. Claims are properly bounded, because a citation is an extraction id and extraction ids come only from admissible sources. This is a rigour gap today rather than an observed failure; it becomes a real one as soon as sections have different ceilings from each other.
items.rootCause: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/src/aer/sections/evidence.py:940-942 builds known_sources from set(evidence.source_tiers) | set(evidence.fact_sources.values()), and evidence.source_tiers is filled at /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/src/aer/sections/evidence.py:708-716 from every source document on the request — deliberately, because the primary-source shortfall check needs it — with no separate set for 'what this section was actually shown'.

items.title: Every run computed the subject's own P/E and EV/EBITDA, and the report has no parameter that can carry them
items.problem: MSFT #1's report says "No discounted cash flow, cost of equity ... value per share or peer multiple sits on this record" and §17 says "No comparable figure was computed". Both are false about the run. The comps step recorded the subject's P/E at 27.43x, EV/EBITDA 18.93x, EV/Sales 11.08x and P/B 8.27x, each a traced calculation replayed with zero divergence. AZN recorded P/E 24.49x; M&T recorded P/E 14.11x. Not one of those figures appears in any of the five reports. The operator can see them only on the internal valuation page. Six of six judges said the figures a research note is read for are withheld; one wrote that a note holding EPS, net income and a price series but reporting no multiple "has not run out of inputs".
items.rootCause: The render path is typed so that a multiple cannot pass through it. `assemble_document` takes `comps: WithheldComps | None` (src/aer/render/document.py:436) and its module docstring states the intent: "a caller wanting to put the numbers in a report cannot do it by passing a different argument — there is no argument that would carry them" (src/aer/render/document.py:5-10). The only thing that reaches the document is one string, `comps.as_paragraph()` (src/aer/render/document.py:587). That signature enforces ADR 0030 route 2 as it stood before its own 2026-08-09 amendment: the fetch policy now says `derived_figures_publishable=True` (src/aer/fetch/policy.py:192) and `CompsTable.for_audience` honours it (src/aer/calc/comps.py:314-315), but the render boundary never receives a `CompsTable` to ask. Separately, no section writer is given the table at all: grepping `comps` across src/aer/sections/ returns nothing but the unrelated `exit_multiple` assumption.
evidence: audit/out/msft1/run-export.json — comps step output `subject_multiples`: ev_ebitda 18.92530579440600915376576038550843, ev_sales 11.07764494706, pe 27.43398328690, p_b 8.26731318958

Let the assembler accept `CompsTable | WithheldComps` and have the caller pass `table.for_audience(Audience.SHAREABLE)`, which already returns the table when the policy permits and the withheld notice when it does not. Keep ADR 0034's principle exactly: the type still decides, the decision just moves from a hard-coded signature to the licence flag that ADR 0030's amendment set. Do not let a section writer paraphrase them until `multiples-are-unnamed-undated-rows` lands, or the writer will get a number it cannot label.

items.title: A peer is a CIK and a sentence: nothing is acquired for it, so it cannot be dated, aligned, analysed or priced
items.problem: Eight peers are proposed and confirmed on every run and every one is excluded with the same sentence. The gate page tells the operator "Confirming records the set; it fetches nothing", so the platform spends £0.013–£0.016 and a human decision per run on an artefact that contributes no figure, and the report then says the peers were "excluded", which reads to a judge as a verdict on the peers rather than a policy of the tool.
items.rootCause: ADR 0059's first amendment (2026-08-19) withdrew peer acquisition. `peer_discovery._one_peer` returns `PeerProposal(identifier=<CIK>, name=..., rationale=...)` with no `period_end` for any company the database does not already hold (src/aer/services/peer_discovery.py:239-245). `comps.build` then splits on exactly that: every undated peer becomes a `PeerExclusion` carrying `UNACQUIRED_PEER_REASON` (src/aer/services/comps.py:96-98, 542-552). Even if it were dated, `comps_run._one_peer` does `uuid.UUID(str(peer.identifier))` and returns None for a CIK (src/aer/services/comps_run.py:505-507), and `acquire_peer_prices` needs `company.ticker` and `company.exchange` from a Company row that does not exist (src/aer/services/price_acquisition.py:309-312). The amendment's own stated return condition — a price feed — has been met since 2026-09-07; the amendment says re-enabling "remains a decision for the day the feed is subscribed".

items.recommendation: Acquire them — but only after the cheaper items land, and only behind a measured seeding run. The costs are small and now largely measurable: money, none (EDGAR is free, and `CostCategory.DATA_API` is never written anyway, F-06); API allowance, negligible — a peer costs three weighted EODHD calls (eod, splits, dividends) so eight peers cost 24 of a 100,000/day allowance; storage, about 26 MB and 78,000 fact rows for eight peers, which is this repository's own record of the run that once did it; run length, an estimated 1.5–3.5 minutes on a 31–42 minute run — the subject's `acquire` step is 6.6 s and the expensive part of `extract` (156.8 s) is the 18,610 whole-document string searches for excerpts plus the segment sweep, and ADR 0059 skips both for a peer. That last figure is an estimate, not a measurement; the seeding item settles it. The reasons to acquire rather than drop: the comps band is a spine input — `_implied_band` (src/aer/services/comps_run.py:561-625) reads the peer range back onto the subject as two traced implied-value calculations and returned null on every run; the banks profile allows COMPS_MULTIPLES and blocks DCF_FCFF (src/aer/core/sectors.py:152-160), so dropping comps leaves a whole sector class with an allowed model that cannot be built; and the console's own peer tables were judged "ten rows of 'not sourced'" on both subjects — a peer table where every cell is a traced calculation over a hashed filing is the one place the platform can beat the console on the console's own ground. This is §8 item 1 and the call is the operator's; that is my recommendation.

items.title: A second run of the same company on the same day loses its entire price layer, and says the provider returned nothing
items.problem: AZN #2 and M&T both recorded `{"prices": false, "reason": "The market-data provider returned no prices for AZN.US/MTB.US on or before 2026-09-12"}`. The provider returned prices; the platform already held them. The consequence on those two runs was no market capitalisation, no enterprise value, no regressed beta (the operator was asked to type one, with the false explanation "No price history has been acquired for this run"), and no EV multiples. Two of the audit's five runs lost their whole price-derived layer to this, and the run record blames the vendor.
items.rootCause: `_record_listing` returns `bars=stored.inserted` (src/aer/services/price_acquisition.py:477), discarding `StoredBars.already_held` (src/aer/services/prices.py:97, 232). `acquire_prices` then treats `subject.bars == 0` as "the provider returned no prices" and returns early (src/aer/services/price_acquisition.py:208-216). 2026-09-12 was a Saturday, so the last close was Friday's and already stored: MSFT #2 inserted exactly 1 bar and survived; M&T's earlier run at 15:11 inserted 1,514 and the 15:31 re-run inserted 0; AZN's Friday run inserted 1,514 and Saturday's inserted 0. The codebase already gets this right for facts and says so: "the second run of a company inserts nothing, and 'supplied 18588, inserted 0' is the dedupe working" (src/aer/services/facts.py:70-74). `acquire_peer_prices` has the identical bug at line 337, so it would make a peer's multiple silently non-reproducible the moment peers are acquired.
evidence: audit/out/azn2/run-export.json and audit/out/mtb/run-export.json, steps[12].output — `{"prices": false, "reason": "The market-data provider returned no prices for ..."}`
audit/out/msft1 (bars 1513), msft2 (bars 1), azn (1514), mtb-unclassified (1514) acquire_prices outputs
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn2/driver.jsonl and mtb/driver.jsonl — "outstanding beta: supplied by the operator (No price history has been acquired for this run...)"
src/aer/services/price_acquisition.py:208-216, 337-343, 477; src/aer/services/prices.py:93-98, 179-232

Proof the data was there: AZN #2 and M&T still produced subject P/E of 24.49x and 14.11x, because `_subject_price` reads the stored series rather than the step's output (src/aer/services/comps_run.py:430-451)
items.recommendation: Fix it. Count the bars the platform holds for the window, not the bars this run inserted: return `inserted + already_held` from `_Listing`, or better, test `adjusted_series_for(...).bars` — the thing the downstream code actually consumes. Rewrite the refusal so it says what happened ("no usable bar for SYMBOL on or before DATE", which is the peer path's own wording at line 349). items.title: The WACC weights equity at book on every run, including the two that held a market capitalisation, and the report says so
items.problem: Every report that carries a valuation prints: "Book equity was used as the equity weight because no market capitalisation was available ... the equity weight is understated, the debt weight overstated, and the resulting WACC too low. Every valuation discounted at it is correspondingly too high." On MSFT #1 and #2 a market capitalisation was available — $3,656.6bn and $3,680.3bn, recorded as traced calculations in the same run. The document therefore tells a reader that its own headline number is inflated, for a reason untrue of that run. A judge listed exactly this: "MSFT share price and market capitalisation on 11 September 2026 (needed both to compare with the per-share values and to replace the book-value WACC weights)".
items.rootCause: `valuation_run._cost_of_capital` constructs `CapitalStructure(..., basis=EquityBasis.BOOK)` unconditionally, with the now-stale comment "Book, because nothing here acquires a price" (src/aer/services/valuation_run.py:283-289). `acquire_prices` has acquired a price and computed a market capitalisation since 2026-09-07. `EquityBasis.MARKET` exists, is fully supported by `cost_of_capital`, is exercised by fifteen tests, and is constructed nowhere in src/. The caveat attaches automatically whenever the basis is BOOK (src/aer/calc/wacc.py:690).

items.title: All six multiples are recorded under one name, `multiple`, with no period, so they sort last and reach a writer unlabelled
items.problem: The subject's P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA and EV/Sales are persisted as four rows all called `multiple`, all with `period: null`, all `unit: pure`, with nothing distinguishing a 27.43 from an 8.27 but the value itself. A section writer selecting evidence gets `{"name": "multiple", "value": "27.433983286908", "unit": "pure", "period": null}` and cannot tell what it is; and because period-less rows sort last under `period_end.desc().nullslast()`, they are cut by `EVIDENCE_ITEM_CAP = 40` in a run that strikes roughly twenty-four dated ratio rows per period across five periods. So even the path that could have carried a multiple into prose is blocked twice over.
items.rootCause: `@traced(name="multiple", ...)` is a decorator-time constant (src/aer/calc/comps.py:648-652), and `multiples_for` never sets a period scope even though it is handed `period_end` (src/aer/calc/comps.py:775-844). The evidence selector's own comment explains why period-less rows must sort last — the sensitivity grid's hundred-plus period-less cells would otherwise fill the cap (src/aer/sections/evidence.py:572-578) — so the multiples inherit a penalty designed for something else.
evidence: audit/out/msft1/run-export.json — four calculation rows, name "multiple", period null, function_ref aer.calc.comps:multiple, values 27.433983286908 / 8.267313189583 / 18.925305794406 / 11.077644947062; no `parameters` recorded

Either is a contained change inside `aer/calc/comps.py`, which is pure and `mypy --strict`. Note the audit consequence: calculation names are part of the replay record, so this is a code-version boundary — old runs replay against old names, which is what `code_version` is for.

items.title: The eight peers the operator confirmed are not named anywhere in the report
items.problem: MSFT #1's report contains the strings "Alphabet", "Oracle" and "Salesforce" zero times. §17 is one sentence saying eight peers were excluded. items.title: Market capitalisation depends entirely on one filed tag, and the vendor fallback is an endpoint this subscription does not include
items.problem: AZN #1 acquired 1,514 price bars, regressed a beta over 72 observations, and recorded `market_capitalisation: null`. The run log says why: "The fundamentals response for AZN.US is not JSON. An HTML error page or a maintenance notice reaching a parser is a provider outage, not a malformed series." So on a filer whose share count the concept map does not resolve, there is no second route to a market capitalisation at all — and with it no enterprise value, no EV/EBITDA, no EV/Sales, and nothing to cross-check a per-share valuation against, which is exactly what let F-28's depositary-receipt confusion through undetected.
items.rootCause: `_market_capitalisation` prefers the filed count and falls back to `client.fetch_shares_outstanding`, which hits `/api/fundamentals` at weight 10 (src/aer/services/price_acquisition.py:497-512; src/aer/sources/eodhd/client.py:235-259). The workflow's own comment already records that this endpoint "is a feed the operator's subscription does not include, so the fallback could only ever fail" (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2724-2732). The filed route is `_filed_share_count`, one query on concept `shares_outstanding`, unit `shares`, `dimension_axis IS NULL` (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2756-2771). AZN's run did persist a `shares_outstanding` observation for 2025-12-31 — the extract logged a tag collision on it — yet the query returned nothing, which most likely means AZN tags its cover-page count dimensioned by share class and the `dimension_axis IS NULL` filter excludes it. That last step is a hypothesis: the record shows the fallback firing, not which predicate excluded the row.

First, settle the filed-count query: widen `_filed_share_count` to accept a consolidated sum over share classes where the filer dimensions the cover-page count, or state on the row which class it is. Second, add a traced derivation as a last resort — shares = net income / diluted EPS — which is forty lines of Python and is exactly what the judges did by hand on AZN's own page, recorded as a calculation with its two fact inputs so it is as traceable as any other figure. Retire the `/api/fundamentals` call: it costs ten weighted units to fail. This is a modelling definition, so record it. The operator's alternative is buying the fundamentals feed, which the £100/month ceiling in ADR 0030 already argued against.

Widening only the dimension filter may fix nothing. Settle it with one SELECT before writing code — it is the difference between a one-line predicate change and a new traced derivation. Also retire the `/api/fundamentals` call in the same pass regardless of which predicate it was: ten weighted units to fail.

It substitutes a period-average diluted count for an instant, which is F-28's failure in a new place unless the row states the basis — that is a modelling definition and the ADR the item asks for is required, not optional.

items.title: The date a peer is aligned on is not the date its multiple is computed on, and a 45-day window excludes most real comparables
items.problem: Two problems that only appear once peers carry data, and both silently produce a wrong table rather than an empty one. First, `build` aligns a peer on `PeerProposal.period_end` — the newest any fact the platform holds for that company, quarterly instants included — while the multiples are computed from `analyse_company(...).periods[0]`, the newest annual period. A December filer with Q2 data would align on 30 June and be priced on the previous 31 December, and the table would print the June date beside the December multiple. Second, the alignment window is ±45 days, so on a June-year-end subject like Microsoft only a May-year-end peer such as Oracle falls inside it; December, January, September and late-November year ends all fall outside. Acquiring eight peers could therefore buy a one-peer median.
items.rootCause: `peer_discovery._one_peer` and `comps.operator_peers_for_job` both set `period_end = max(FinancialFact.period_end) <= as_of` with no annual restriction (src/aer/services/peer_discovery.py:247-258; src/aer/services/comps.py:357-370), while `comps_run._one_peer` computes from `peer_analysis.periods[0]` (src/aer/services/comps_run.py:512-547) and `build` carries the proposal's date onto the `PeerRow` (src/aer/services/comps.py:556-586). `MAX_PERIOD_DRIFT_DAYS = 45` was chosen to exclude a March-against-December comparison (src/aer/calc/comps.py:74-80) and does that job; it also excludes the ordinary case of a subject whose fiscal year is not December. The fiscal-year-end claims about the eight named peers are general market knowledge, not measured by the audit.
evidence: src/aer/services/peer_discovery.py:247-258; src/aer/services/comps.py:357-370, 542-586; src/aer/services/comps_run.py:512-547

The gate payload declares `"basis": "ttm"` (vertical_slice_v1.py:2444) while the build computes LAST_FISCAL_YEAR (comps_run.py:308, 323)
items.recommendation: Make the aligned date the same date the multiple is computed on — take the peer's latest annual period end from `analyse_company` and align on that, so a row's period and its arithmetic cannot disagree. Then decide the window explicitly: either keep ±45 days and accept that a non-December subject gets a short peer set, with the dates on every row so a reader sees why; or compare on a trailing twelve months, which is what the peer gate's payload already declares and what the comps step then contradicts. Settle the basis mismatch in the same pass.
items.adrSubject: A peer is aligned on the period its multiple is computed from, and what "comparable period" means for a subject whose fiscal year is not the peers' — the 45-day window, or a trailing twelve months.
items.tests: A test that a peer with quarterly facts newer than its last annual period is aligned on the annual date and excluded when that date drifts; a test that `PeerRow.period_end` equals every one of its `MultipleResult.period_end` values; a test that the gate payload's declared basis and the built table's basis are the same value.

items.challengeNote: Split the item. Making the aligned date equal the date the multiples were computed from is a correctness fix with no decision in it — an hour, no ADR, and it should ship immediately because it already bites the only peers that can be priced today (a previously researched company). Only the window question (45 days vs trailing twelve months) is the operator's and needs the ADR. As written, a one-line bug fix is held hostage to a modelling decision. Add the consequence the item misses: because a seeded peer's proposal date comes from all facts including quarterly periods and cover-page instants, a company researched shortly before the run carries a date near the as-of date — for MSFT's 2026-06-30 subject period that is typically 46-75 days of drift, i.e. exclusion before pricing.

items.title: The priced-peer chain can be proved end to end today, for about £30 and no code change
items.problem: Every part of the peer-multiple argument rests on estimates: how long a peer's acquisition takes, whether the alignment holds, whether a real peer's multiples are sane, whether the evidence pool stays clean. Nothing in the audit measured any of it, because no run has ever had a priced peer. Committing two to three sessions to peer acquisition on estimates is the expensive way to find out.
items.rootCause: Not a defect — an opportunity the current design already allows and nobody has used. `peer_discovery._one_peer` looks the resolved CIK up in `companies` and, when it finds a row, returns the company's UUID and its latest stored period instead of a bare CIK (src/aer/services/peer_discovery.py:239-258). From there `comps_run._one_peer` parses the UUID, analyses the company, and prices it through `acquire_peer_prices` using the ticker and exchange `upsert_company` stored when that company was itself a subject. A company the platform has already researched is already a fully priceable peer, with no change to any file.

That is roughly £21–£30 of live spend and it settles, with real data, every open question in this area at once: how the alignment behaves, whether the peer's facts stay out of the subject's evidence pool under ADR 0061, how long a peer's analysis and pricing actually take, and whether the resulting multiples are sane. It also produces the first comps table this platform has ever built, which is the thing to put in front of a judge. items.title: The two sector-specialist multiples can never be computed, for the subject or any peer
items.problem: M&T's comps row reports "the filing does not report tangible_book_value_per_share for this period", and so does every other run for P/TBV and P/FFO. The banks profile names `tangible_book_value_per_share` as a required metric and allows COMPS_MULTIPLES while blocking the DCF, and `specialist_multiples_for('banks')` exists precisely to put P/TBV in front of a reader first. The denominator is never produced anywhere, so a bank — the sector for which comparables are the sanctioned route — can never get the multiple the platform itself says is the right one. The same holds for a REIT and P/FFO.
items.rootCause: `comps_run._inputs_for` builds revenue, ebitda, earnings_per_share, shares_outstanding, book_value_per_share, price_per_share, market_capitalisation, net_debt and enterprise_value — and nothing else (src/aer/services/comps_run.py:342-413). `tangible_book_value_per_share` and `ffo_per_share` appear only as denominator names in `MULTIPLE_DEFINITIONS` (src/aer/calc/comps.py:503-524), so `multiples_for` reports them absent every time, correctly and permanently.
evidence: audit/out/mtb/run-export.json and every other run — `p_tbv` absent_because "the filing does not report tangible_book_value_per_share for this period"
src/aer/services/comps_run.py:342-413; src/aer/calc/comps.py:503-524, 673-690; src/aer/services/comps.py:648-664 (`specialist_multiples_for`)
src/aer/core/sectors.py:152-170 — banks: allowed_models includes COMPS_MULTIPLES, blocked_models includes DCF_FCFF, required_metrics includes tangible_book_value_per_share

The tangible-book definition is a choice — which intangibles come out, and whether preferred stock and non-controlling interests do, which §8 item 8 already flags as open for a bank's opening book value — so it needs recording rather than inventing. Sequence it after §8 item 2 (a bank's revenue) is decided, because a bank with no approvable report has nowhere to show a P/TBV.

Narrow the property test too: "P/TBV is at least P/B whenever intangibles are positive" holds only while tangible book stays positive — a bank whose goodwill exceeds equity gives a non-positive denominator and `multiple` (calc/comps.py:678-690) refuses, which is the correct behaviour and would fail the property as stated.

items.title: Half the proposed peers are foreign issuers priced as depositary receipts, and a multiple over them is wrong in a way no check would catch
items.problem: Of the eight peers proposed for AZN — Pfizer, Merck, BMS, Lilly, Novartis, Sanofi, GSK, J&J — four are foreign private issuers whose US listing is a depositary receipt over a fraction or multiple of an ordinary share, and some report in a currency other than the price's. A P/E computed as US receipt price over earnings per ordinary share is arithmetically clean, plausible in the output, and wrong by the receipt ratio. This is F-28 repeated once per peer, and unlike F-28 there is no market capitalisation on the row to cross-check against. SAP appears in the MSFT set for the same reason.
items.rootCause: Currency is protected: `multiple` refuses a non-dimensionless result and `comps_run._one_peer` catches the resulting `AerError` and drops the peer with a logged reason (src/aer/calc/comps.py:689-700; src/aer/services/comps_run.py:548-552), so a EUR-reporting, USD-priced peer is excluded correctly. The depositary-ratio problem is not protected at all: an ADR priced in USD over EPS reported in USD is dimensionally perfect and numerically wrong. The platform holds no receipt ratio for any listing, which §8 item 3 already records as reference data it has no source for. `resolve_entity` returns the EDGAR exchange (src/aer/sources/sec/tickers.py:47-57) and `market_proxy_for` covers only NASDAQ, NYSE and LSE (src/aer/sources/eodhd/proxies.py:69-102), so a peer on NYSE American, Cboe or OTC is refused with a reason — the right outcome, and worth knowing before it surprises somebody.
evidence: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn/gate-PEER_SET.json — NOVARTIS AG (0001114448), Sanofi (0001121404), GSK plc (0001131399); msft1 — SAP SE (0001000184)
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md F-28 and §8 item 3 — "one NYSE ADR is half an ordinary share, so $169.80 is either roughly fair value or 100 % upside"
src/aer/calc/comps.py:689-700; src/aer/services/comps_run.py:548-552; src/aer/sources/eodhd/proxies.py:69-144; src/aer/sources/sec/tickers.py:44-110
items.recommendation: Whatever §8 item 3 decides for the subject must be decided for a peer at the same time, and the safe default is to exclude rather than guess: refuse a peer whose EDGAR filing status is foreign private issuer (20-F/40-F) unless a receipt ratio is held, and say so on the exclusion row. A short exclusion list reading "priced as a depositary receipt; this platform holds no receipt ratio for it" is a better peer set than a longer one with two rows silently out by a factor of two. Nothing here should be built until `peers-recorded-by-cik-nothing-fetched` is decided; it is a precondition of that item rather than a separate gain.
items.tests: A test that a peer whose filings are 20-F and whose listing is a depositary receipt is excluded by name with the receipt reason; a test that a peer reporting in a currency other than its quote currency is excluded with the unit mismatch stated rather than raising the run.
items.acceptance: On a seeded AZN run with acquired peers, the excluded list distinguishes "reports in another currency", "priced as a depositary receipt" and "period would not align" as three separate reasons, and no multiple on the table mixes a receipt price with an ordinary-share denominator.

That is a smaller but sharper claim, and it makes the proposed default — exclude 20-F/40-F filers until a ratio is held — proportionate rather than a set-halving rule. Keep it as a precondition of acquisition, as the item says.

items.title: The peer gate and the comps disclosure still tell the operator the figures will be withheld, which the licence determination reversed a month before the audit
items.problem: The peer-set gate's callout reads "These figures do not leave this machine ... licensed market data whose terms grant no derived-data exemption ... a shareable report carries a note that it was performed and withholds the figures." The comps disclosure's other branch says "The figures are withheld from this version." Both state the position ADR 0030 route 2 held before its own 2026-08-09 amendment. An operator reading the gate is told that confirming a peer set buys a report that withholds the result — so the gate argues against the work this whole area is about. F-25 already found one ADR-flavoured sentence leaking into a report's withheld-figure note; this is the same stale text in two more places.
items.rootCause: The determination moved in one place — `derived_figures_publishable=True` on the EODHD policy (src/aer/fetch/policy.py:187-192) — and `CompsTable.for_audience` reads it (src/aer/calc/comps.py:314). The two prose surfaces hard-code the old answer: src/aer/web/templates/runs/peers.html:27-33 and the peers-present branch of `WithheldComps.as_paragraph` (src/aer/calc/comps.py:399-415). No test binds either to the flag, unlike the licence note itself, which `tests/test_fetch_policy.py::TestTheEodhdLicenceNote` holds against it.

Reword the gate to say what confirming actually buys once the other items land. Small, but it is on the one page where the operator decides whether the peer set is worth their attention.

The proposed test cannot be written where the item puts it: `WithheldComps.as_paragraph` is reached only after the withholding decision has been taken, so asserting it "does not claim figures are withheld when the policy permits" is vacuous — the binding test belongs at the call site that chooses between the table and the notice, i.e. `comps_note_for`, which must start consulting `for_audience`. items.title: The store holds segment revenue and no section writer is allowed to see it
items.problem: The Segment Analysis section states, in the same report and on the same PDF page as a chart of the three segments' revenue, that "no segment-level dollar figures or a currency-denominated Microsoft Cloud aggregate were available to cite here". The section's `segments` figure array — which its own contract provides — comes back empty on every run. All three judges scored "segment revenue breakdown for the latest fiscal year" as absent against a console note that printed PBP $139,996m / IC $137,791m / MPC $54,052m.
items.rootCause: `visible_facts` is the single door every section's evidence pack uses, and it filters `FinancialFact.dimension_axis.is_(None)` — src/aer/services/facts.py:88, the rule ADR 0058 wrote as "section evidence packs ... filter on dimension_axis IS NULL". `aer/sections/evidence.py:511` calls it for the `search_facts` category, so the drafter of segment_analysis is handed only consolidated rows. The writer is not hallucinating an absence; it is reporting one accurately. ADR 0058's own consequences already anticipate the repair: "A future consumer that *wants* segment rows (a segment-analysis section, interim segment trends) selects them explicitly by axis; nothing reaches them by accident." Nobody has written that consumer.
evidence: src/aer/services/facts.py:86-95 — `visible_facts` hard-filters `dimension_axis IS NULL`, docstring "Consolidated only, under ADR 0058"
src/aer/sections/evidence.py:505-524 — the only fact query a section pack runs, via `visible_facts`

items.recommendation: Add a third evidence category — call it `search_segment_facts` — selected explicitly by axis and period, enabled only on the section definitions that declare it (segment_analysis first, business_overview second). Every unit's `internal` payload must carry `dimension_axis` and `dimension_member` so the figure can never read as the company's own line, which is the condition ADR 0058 attached. The figure rows the writer emits then cite `financial_fact_id`, the convention section_output.py:625 calls "the figure-row convention every built-in section has used since Phase 1", so invariant 3 is satisfied with no new machinery and no arithmetic in a prompt. Do not compute shares or growth in the writer: if segment growth is wanted, it is a `aer.calc` function writing calculation rows, exactly as the consolidated ratios are.
items.adrSubject: None new: ADR 0058's consequences already authorise a consumer that selects dimensioned rows explicitly. It needs an amendment note recording the first such consumer and the rule that a dimensioned figure must carry its axis and member wherever it is presented.

A second test asserts a dimensioned unit is never emitted without `dimension_member`.

items.invariantRisk: ADR 0058's Decision names "section evidence packs" explicitly among the readers that must filter `dimension_axis IS NULL`; only the Consequences authorise a later consumer. The item is right that no new ADR is needed, but the amendment note is mandatory, not optional — a change to one of the four places the Decision names, left unrecorded, is a silent ADR breach. The amendment must also state the rendering rule (axis and member carried wherever a dimensioned figure is shown), because that is the condition the Decision attaches, and `covered_figures` (evidence.py:815-836) will accept a dimensioned fact id as cover for any numeral without knowing it is a slice.

items.title: The one place segment revenue reaches a reader is a bar chart with no values, dropped from the Markdown edition
items.problem: MSFT #1's PDF has a real segment chart — "Segment mix — FY2026", three bars labelled Productivity And Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, More Personal Computing, against an axis running to 140 USDbn — and not one printed figure. A reader can eyeball "about 140" and no more. The Markdown edition, which is what the six judges were handed and what a reader gets outside the interface, replaces the whole exhibit with the line "*Rendered in the HTML and PDF editions of this report.*". All three judges called it a "placeholder"; it was not a placeholder, it was a chart they could not see.
items.rootCause: `segment_mix` draws `axis.barh(...)` and sets a title and an x-label, and never calls `bar_label` or writes any value text — src/aer/charts/builders.py:120-165. The Markdown notation deliberately defers geometry: src/aer/render/markdown.py:249-256 emits title, caption, markers and a deferral line. The caption itself proves the data was there: a placeholder's caption is its message and carries no citations (builders.py:475-482), while msft1/report.md:111 reads "Revenue by reported segment, FY2026.[^23][^24][^25]" with three citations to msft-20260630.htm. So the figures existed, were cited, were drawn, and were never written down.

Also ADR 0043's consequence 5 asserts the Markdown notation carries "each exhibit's caption and markers" and that "the figures resolve in both notations" — adding a table amends consequence 5 as well as 4, and consequence 5's claim that the figures already resolve is the sentence the judges disproved.

items.title: The segment exhibit disappears the second time a company is researched
items.problem: MSFT #1 and AZN #1 both rendered a segment chart. MSFT #2 and AZN #2 — the same two companies re-commissioned against the same database — have no "### Segment mix" heading at all, and no segment exhibit in any edition. The refresh use case, which the audit calls "yes, once fixed", silently loses the only surface segment revenue ever reached.
items.rootCause: `_segment_input` joins `SourceDocument.job_id == job.id` (src/aer/services/exhibits.py:337) while facts are inserted idempotently on an observation key that excludes the source document — src/aer/services/facts.py:170-215, and the rationale is spelled out at facts.py:76-80: "the *second* run of a company inserts nothing, and 'supplied 18588, inserted 0' is the dedupe working. Those rows hang off the first run's document." So run two's exhibit query sees none of run one's rows. An empty input renders the placeholder, and `exportable_charts_for` drops every placeholder from the report outright (exhibits.py:127-129), so the exhibit does not degrade — it disappears. `_revenue_margin_input` (exhibits.py:197) has the same join and survives only because the aggregate re-inserts under the new job. The corroborating detail: AZN #2 wrote 65 new segment facts (the ten IFRS tags F-12 newly mapped), none of them `concept == "revenue"`, so the query's other predicates finished the job.

src/aer/services/facts.py:76-80 and 170-215 — facts deduplicate on an observation key excluding the source document; "the second run of a company inserts nothing"
