items.recommendation: Scope the exhibit query the way ADR 0061 scoped everything else: by company and the run's point-in-time window, not by job. `visible_facts` already encodes exactly that policy for consolidated rows and the same predicates apply here — company, and `filed_date <= as_of_date` under point-in-time. Apply the same correction to `_revenue_margin_input` at exhibits.py:197, which carries the same latent bug. This also closes the gap between the exhibit's rows and the section's rows once the first item lands: both should read the same door.
items.tests: tests/test_exhibits.py::TestASecondRunStillDrawsTheSegments — segment facts stored against job A's source document; `exportable_charts_for` called with job B for the same company returns a non-placeholder `segment_mix`. Paired with a point-in-time test: a fact filed after job B's as-of date is not drawn.
items.acceptance: Re-running the exhibit assembly against MSFT #2's and AZN #2's stored rows produces the same segment chart their first runs produced, with the same citations. The refresh use case (§4.3 row 2) renders the same exhibits as the first run.

options.name: Scope by company and as-of date
options.change: Replace the job join with the `visible_facts`-style predicates, lifting the `dimension_axis IS NULL` clause for this consumer.
options.risk: Very low; it is the scoping rule ADR 0061 already settled.

options.name: Re-persist under each job
options.change: Make the sweep write a per-job provenance row even when the fact already exists.
options.risk: Duplicates provenance and fights the idempotency ADR 0058 relies on. Not recommended.

items.challengeNote: Two corrections, both raising the item. (1) The claim that `_revenue_margin_input` "survives only because the aggregate re-inserts under the new job" is refuted: msft2 wrote zero facts, and its revenue-and-margin exhibit cites [^36]-[^50], fifteen markers that are all `Calculated:` footnotes — five periods of three margins and no revenue bars at all — against msft1's twenty-one markers, of which [^36]-[^41] are companyfacts source documents. azn2 ([^39]-[^53], all calculations) and mtb ([^14]-[^18]) are the same. The chart survives because margin *calculations* are written per job; the revenue bars are lost exactly as the segments are, under a caption that still reads "Every bar and point is a stored figure" (builders.py:112-116). That is a false sentence in three of the five approved reports, not a latent bug, and it belongs in the acceptance. (2) The bank is a third instance the item missed: mtb-unclassified's extract wrote 23,174 facts and 182 segment facts; the mtb re-run wrote 0 and 0 and drew no segment exhibit. So 182 stored segment rows for M&T were never drawn either. Effort: "an hour" holds for the join itself, but `RevenueMarginInput.is_empty` (src/aer/charts/model.py:84-85) returns False when only margins survive, so the caption/empty rule needs fixing too — call it a session.
items.invariantRisk: None, and it removes one. Re-scoping to company plus `filed_date <= as_of_date` is the ADR 0061 rule `visible_facts` already encodes, and it restores point-in-time to a query that currently has no date predicate at all. Lifting `dimension_axis IS NULL` for this one consumer is the same ADR 0058 amendment item 1 needs — do it once, in one note.

items.title: On an IFRS filer the "segment" exhibit draws geography, mixes subtotals with parts, and never reaches therapy area or product
items.problem: AstraZeneca's segment exhibit drew eighteen bars: "Outside United Kingdom", "Ifrs Americas", "US", "Europe Excluding United Kingdom", "Asia Africa And Australasia", "CN", "GB", "JP", "DE", "SE", "FR", "ES", "IT", "CA", "AU", "Other Asia Africa And Australasia Excluding Australia China And Japan" and more — region subtotals and ISO country codes on one axis, with labels long enough to squeeze the plot. It is not a segment mix; it is an unreadable geography chart. Meanwhile the judges' repeated complaint about AZN was "no product-level revenue", and the brief's first focus question is patent-expiry exposure by product.
items.rootCause: `_SEGMENT_AXES` lists three axes, all US-GAAP or SRT: `us-gaap:StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis`, `srt:ProductOrServiceAxis`, `srt:StatementGeographicalAxis` (src/aer/services/exhibits.py:313-317). An IFRS filer's axes match none of them, so exhibits.py:358 falls through to `min(axes)` — an alphabetical tie-break that decides what the exhibit *is*, which is exactly the failure mode the constant's own comment says the preference order exists to prevent. The run's own research worker recorded that the breakdown is there: "The FY2025 20-F XBRL data breaks out revenue by therapy area (Oncology, Cardiovascular & Metabolic Diseases, Respiratory, Rare Diseases, Vaccines & Immune Therapies) and by geography". `ifrs-full:Revenue` maps to `revenue` (src/aer/core/concepts.py:398), so those rows are persistable. `_without_subtotals` recognises an aggregate only by exact arithmetic equality, which a partially-tagged geography hierarchy does not satisfy.
evidence: src/aer/services/exhibits.py:308-317 — `_SEGMENT_AXES`, comment: "Deterministic preference rather than 'most members' because the axis chosen decides what the exhibit *is*"
src/aer/services/exhibits.py:358 — `axis = next((name for name in _SEGMENT_AXES if name in axes), min(axes))`
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn/report.pdf — the eighteen-bar geography chart; docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn/report.md:110 cites footnotes 20–37 for it
src/aer/core/concepts.py:395-399 — `IFRS_ALIASES["Revenue"] = "revenue"`
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn2/run-export.json — research_company finding: the 20-F XBRL "breaks out revenue by therapy area ... and by geography"
src/aer/services/exhibits.py:429-440 — `_without_subtotals` recognises an aggregate only by exact arithmetic
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md §4.1 (line 318) — the AZN judges: "there is no product-level revenue"
items.recommendation: Extend the preference list with the IFRS equivalents (the reportable-segment axis first, then the products-and-services axis, then geography), and make the fallback refuse rather than guess: when no axis in the run's rows matches a known preference, name the axes found in the placeholder message rather than picking one alphabetically. That converts a wrong chart into an honest gap and a diagnosis the operator can act on. Separately, treat a member whose value exceeds the sum of the others on the same axis as a suspected subtotal — today only exact equality is caught, and hierarchical geography never meets it.
items.tests: tests/test_exhibits.py::TestAnIfrsFilerSegmentsByItsOwnSegments — rows on both an IFRS segments axis and an IFRS geographical axis produce a chart drawn on the segments axis; and ::TestAnUnknownAxisIsNotGuessed — rows on an axis in no preference list produce a placeholder that names the axes found, not a chart.
items.acceptance: Re-running the exhibit builder over AZN's stored rows draws either the therapy-area axis, or an honest placeholder naming the axes it found — never eighteen mixed geography bars. The country-code members disappear from the document.

options.name: Extend the preference list and refuse the fallback
options.change: Add IFRS axes; replace `min(axes)` with a placeholder that names what it found.
options.risk: An IFRS filer using an entity-extension axis for its segments still gets nothing — but it gets an honest nothing that says which axis to add.

options.name: Let the operator choose the axis at a gate
options.change: Show the axes found and their member counts at the unmapped-concepts gate and let the operator pick.
options.cost: A few sessions; a new gate payload and page.
options.risk: Adds a seventh decision to a run that already has six. Probably worse for issue 1.

items.challengeNote: (a) AstraZeneca has one reportable segment. The platform's own report says so from the 20-F: "AstraZeneca discloses only a single reportable operating segment … does not monitor profitability by individual product, brand or drug class" (azn/report.md:106). Adding an IFRS reportable-segment axis at the head of the preference list therefore cannot produce a therapy-area chart for this filer; the honest outcome is one bar or the placeholder. The item's acceptance already allows that, but its problem statement ("never reaches therapy area or product") sells a fix that the filer's own disclosure forecloses — the therapy-area rows, if they exist, are on an entity-extension axis nothing on any preference list will match. (b) The proposed subtotal heuristic — "a member whose value exceeds the sum of the others on the same axis is a suspected subtotal" — is unsound and should be dropped. Any company with one segment above half of revenue meets it, so the rule would silently delete the largest genuine segment. `_without_subtotals` (exhibits.py:429-440) chose exact arithmetic precisely so that "the consequence of a wrong drop is a missing bar, never a wrong number"; the replacement inverts that property. If hierarchical geography must be handled, handle it by member hierarchy or by refusing the axis, not by magnitude.
items.invariantRisk: The magnitude heuristic, not the axis list. Dropping the biggest real segment produces a chart whose bars are stored facts but whose composition is a deterministic fiction — it does not breach invariant 3 on any single figure, and that is exactly why no check would catch it.

items.title: The platform downloaded the 8-K cover page and left the exhibit that holds the numbers beside it
items.problem: MSFT #1's report says "A current report dated September 2026 falls inside the point-in-time window, but its substance is not before us", and cites the 8-K anyway. The console's note built its entire segment table, its FY25 comparatives, its quarterly progression, and its single most important claim — "operating margin declined in each successive quarter of FY26, from 48.9% in Q1 to 45.1% in Q4" — from source [S5]. [S5] is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000789019/000119312526380280/d291965dex991.htm. The platform fetched https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/789019/000119312526380280/d291965d8k.htm. Same accession, same folder, same filing date, same T1 tier, same already-allowed host. One file apart.
items.rootCause: `Filing.url()` composes the archive path from the CIK and the accession and appends `primary_document` and nothing else — src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:82-91. `Filing.to_ref()` builds the one reference the acquisition layer ever receives (submissions.py:93-106), and `SecClient.discover_documents` selects only filings that *have* a primary document and returns one ref each (src/aer/sources/sec/client.py:235-256). Nothing anywhere reads a filing's index — no `{accession}/index.json`, no `-index.htm`, no exhibit list. For an 8-K this is structurally fatal: the primary document of an 8-K is a cover page whose entire content is a sentence saying the information is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. `_regions` correctly reads an 8-K whole (filings.py:544-553); there is simply nothing in it to read.
evidence: src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:82-91 — `Filing.url()` returns "the URL of this filing's primary document"
src/aer/sources/sec/client.py:235-256 — `discover_documents` yields one `DocumentRef` per filing, from `primary_document`
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/report.md:696 and :712 — the platform's 8-K artefact is `.../000119312526380280/d291965d8k.htm`
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/baseline/msft1/note.md:645 — "[S5] Microsoft Corp, Form 8-K Exhibit 99.1 — 'Segment History as Reported' ... /000119312526380280/d291965dex991.htm"
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/baseline/msft1/note.md:69, :170, :178, :587-588 — the console's segment table, quarterly progression and cross-foot checks all cite [S5]
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/report.md:342 — "A current report dated September 2026 falls inside the point-in-time window, but its substance is not before us."
src/aer/fetch/policy.py:128 — `allowed_hosts=(".sec.gov",)`: the exhibit needs no allowlist change
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md §4.3 row 6 — "MSFT's 8-K of 2 September 2026 is cited, its substance 'not before us'"
items.recommendation: Read the accession's file index and acquire its exhibits alongside the primary document, bounded and typed: EX-99.x for a current report, and the financial-statement exhibits for a periodic one. The point-in-time rule is untouched — every file in an accession carries the accession's filing date, which is already what `to_ref` uses. The fetch layer, the hashing, the excerpting and the citation verifier all work unchanged; only the reference list grows. Bound it hard (one extra index read per filing, the exhibit files only, a size cap) so the cost stays inside the £10 target — the audit's runs averaged £7.19, and these are fetches, not model calls. This is the highest-leverage single change in this area: it is the same document the console won on, in a folder the platform already opened.
items.adrSubject: An accession is a set of documents, not one: acquisition fetches a filing's exhibits as well as its primary document, which ones, and how each is dated and tiered.
items.tests: tests/test_filings.py::TestAnEightKBringsItsExhibit — a replayed accession index containing `d291965d8k.htm` and `d291965dex991.htm` yields two source documents, both dated the filing date, both T1, with excerpts recorded from the exhibit; and ::TestExhibitsAreBoundedAndTyped — a filing with forty exhibits acquires only the typed, capped subset.
items.acceptance: A replayed MSFT run acquires `d291965dex991.htm`, records excerpts from it, and the Recent Developments and Segment Analysis sections cite it. The sentence "its substance is not before us" does not appear. Run cost stays under £8.

options.name: Read the accession index and take typed exhibits
options.change: One extra fetch per acquired filing; select EX-99.x on current reports, add the primary document's siblings on periodic ones.
options.cost: A few sessions plus an ADR. A handful of extra fetches per run, no model spend.
options.risk: More bytes and more excerpts competing for pack budget — mitigated by the excerpt caps that already exist.

options.name: Reach exhibits through EDGAR full-text search only
options.change: Let a research worker find the exhibit with `search_filings_full_text`, which already exists and is already scoped to the CIK, and fetch it with `fetch_known_url`.
options.cost: Nearly free — the tools are built (src/aer/services/research.py:229-300).
options.risk: Non-deterministic: it depends on a worker choosing to search and on its twelve-call budget, which AZN #2's own workers reported exhausting. Good as a supplement, not as the mechanism.

options.name: Leave it
options.change: Nothing.
options.risk: Guidance, recast segment histories and every quarterly results release stay permanently out of reach, and the console keeps winning on all three.

items.challengeNote: "The fetch layer, the hashing, the excerpting and the citation verifier all work unchanged; only the reference list grows" is true and insufficient. EX-99.1 is an untagged HTML press release: `aer.extract.html` produces text only, there is no table-to-rows extractor anywhere in src/aer/extract/, and the segment dollars live in a table. Numeric claims are gated by `covered_figures` (src/aer/sections/evidence.py:815-836) — every sound numeric claim must carry a `financial_fact_id` or a `calculation_id` — so a figure that exists only inside an excerpt cannot be printed at all. Acquiring the exhibit therefore buys the guidance *sentences*, the recent-developments prose and the removal of "its substance is not before us"; it does not and cannot produce the console's PBP $139,996m / IC $137,791m / MPC $54,052m table, nor the 48.9%-to-45.1% progression, which is arithmetic over that table. The acceptance criterion should be cut to "the exhibit is acquired, excerpted and cited", and the segment dollars re-routed to item 1's XBRL path. "Decisive" is right for guidance and recent developments and wrong for segments; "a few sessions" holds only for the fetch, with a separate and larger piece if a filing table is ever to become facts.
items.invariantRisk: None introduced — every file in an accession carries the accession's filing date, which is already what `to_ref` uses, so point-in-time is untouched. But the ADR the item calls for must say what happens to figures read from an exhibit's tables, or the next session will try to let a writer quote one.

items.title: The five current reports a run reads are the five most recent, so housekeeping crowds out results
items.problem: AstraZeneca's second run acquired six documents: the 20-F and five 6-Ks. Three of the five are "Admission of Further Securities to Trading", "Total Voting Rights" and "Admission to Trading — EUR2.55 billion Bond Offering". The company's half-year results announcement, which is where an FPI states its guidance, was not among them. The run's own recent-developments worker then recorded, as a lead it could not follow: "Numerous recent 6-K filings were identified in the source listing but not fetched/read for competitive content".
items.rootCause: `_wanted` sorts current reports by `(filing_date, accession)` descending and takes the first `MAX_CURRENT_REPORTS` — src/aer/services/filings.py:353-357, with the cap at filings.py:70. Nothing looks at what the filing is about. EDGAR states exactly that in the submissions index: the `items` column is listed among `_OPTIONAL_COLUMNS` at src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:61-67 and is then discarded — the `Filing` dataclass (submissions.py:70-81) has no `items` field and the parser (submissions.py:230-243) never sets one. Item 2.02 is "Results of Operations and Financial Condition"; the platform reads the column that says so and throws it away.
evidence: src/aer/services/filings.py:353-357 — `current = sorted(..., key=lambda item: (item.filing_date, item.accession), reverse=True)[:max_current]`
src/aer/services/filings.py:70 — `MAX_CURRENT_REPORTS: Final = 5`
src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:61-67 — `"items"` is requested from the index
src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:70-81, 230-243 — `Filing` has no `items` field and the parser never populates one
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn2/run-export.json — acquire step: five 6-Ks, three of them admission/voting-rights notices
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn2/run-export.json — research_industry lead: "Numerous recent 6-K filings were identified in the source listing but not fetched/read"
src/aer/services/filings.py:62-65 — the CURRENT_FORMS comment names "a guidance change" as the reason current reports are read at all
items.recommendation: Keep `items` on `Filing` and select current reports by materiality before recency: always take the most recent Item 2.02 (results) and Item 7.01 (Reg FD) filings within the window, then fill the remaining slots by date. A 6-K has no item codes, so for a foreign private issuer use the index's `primaryDocDescription`, which already carries the RNS headline the run records as the title ('IMFINZI+IMDELLTRA IMPROVED OS...', 'TOTAL VOTING RIGHTS'), and prefer the results announcements by a small keyword list in the spirit of `_WORTH_READING`. Deterministic, no model call, no extra fetch. This item is worth little alone and a great deal in combination with the exhibit fetch: together they are what puts a results release and its guidance in front of a section.
items.tests: tests/test_filings.py::TestAResultsReleaseOutranksAVotingRightsNotice — an index with six current reports, the results one fifth by date, acquires the results one; and ::TestTheItemCodesSurviveParsing — `Filing.items` round-trips from the index payload.
items.acceptance: A replayed AZN acquisition brings back the half-year results 6-K; a replayed MSFT acquisition brings back the Q4 results 8-K. The recent-developments worker's "identified but not fetched" lead disappears.

options.name: Rank by item code, then by date
options.change: Keep `items`; reserve slots for Item 2.02 / 7.01 and for description-matched 6-Ks.
options.risk: A filer that mis-codes an item loses its slot to date order, which is today's behaviour anyway.

options.name: Raise the cap
options.change: Take ten or fifteen current reports instead of five.
options.cost: An hour; more fetches and more excerpts.
options.risk: Crude: it buys coverage by spending the excerpt pool on more housekeeping, and `_EXCERPT_POOL` (200) starts to bind.

items.challengeNote: Every claim checks out. `_wanted` sorts current reports by `(filing_date, accession)` descending and truncates (src/aer/services/filings.py:353-357) with `MAX_CURRENT_REPORTS: Final = 5` at :70, and the CURRENT_FORMS comment at :62-65 names "a guidance change" as the reason they are read. `"items"` sits in `_OPTIONAL_COLUMNS` (src/aer/sources/sec/submissions.py:61-67) and is copied into `columns` by `_validated_columns` (:265-268), then never read: `Filing` (:70-81) has no `items` field and the parser (:233-243) never sets one. The column really is read and thrown away. azn2's acquire step lists the 20-F plus five 6-Ks, of which ADMISSION OF FURTHER SECURITIES TO TRADING, TOTAL VOTING RIGHTS and ADMISSION TO TRADING - EUR2.55 BILLION BOND OFFERING are housekeeping, and the descriptions confirm `primaryDocDescription` carries the RNS headline the item wants to match on. A session is right.
items.invariantRisk: None. Selection by item code is deterministic Python over a regulator's own index; no model call, no new fetch, no change to point-in-time.

items.title: Nothing in the system knows what management guidance is, and the two doors to it are shut
items.problem: "Management guidance or outlook for the coming period" is scored absent by all three judges on the platform's MSFT note and present-sourced on the console's, which printed a ten-row FY27 outlook table. The platform's Growth Outlook section wants guidance — its excerpt keywords include "guidance", "outlook", "backlog", "obligation" — and has no document in front of it that contains any.
items.rootCause: Three independent reasons, in order of bite. First, guidance for a US domestic filer is not in the 10-K at all: it is stated on the earnings call and in the results release exhibit, and the platform fetches neither (see the exhibit item; the earnings call is not an SEC filing at all). Second, the tier-2 door is built and unwired: `aer.sources.issuer.discover_documents` — "annual report PDFs, results presentations, transcripts" — has no caller anywhere in `src/`, only in tests/test_discovery.py. This is F-04's shape exactly, a second time. Third, even a secondary source would not reach a section: every built-in section's evidence policy sets `max_tier: T4_LICENSED_MARKET` and `requires_primary: True` (migrations/versions/0023:43-48), enforced at src/aer/sections/evidence.py:634, which is F-21's "News and web sources never reach a built-in section". And there is no `guidance` field in any section contract and no guidance concept anywhere in the code — the word appears in `src/aer/` only as operator/skill guidance.
evidence: migrations/versions/0029_sections_declare_their_evidence_preferences.py:169-172 — growth_outlook's excerpt keywords include "guidance", "outlook", "backlog", "obligation"
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/report.md:330-342 — Growth Outlook contains no guidance; its closing sentence is "its substance is not before us"

docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/judges/reads.json — msft1 doc-A operator: "no figures, no quarter, no earnings-call guidance"; doc-B operator: "§12 table 'FY27 outlook — what management has actually guided'"
src/aer/sources/issuer.py:1-30, 167 — the tier-2 IR adapter; `discover_documents` has no caller in src/ (only tests/test_discovery.py:35)
migrations/versions/0023_the_eighteen_section_spine.py:43-48 — `_EVIDENCE_POLICY` = max_tier T4, requires_primary True, applied to every spine section
src/aer/sections/evidence.py:634 — `source.source_tier.rank <= policy.max_tier_rank`
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md F-21 — "News and web sources never reach a built-in section: every built-in section's tier ceiling is T4 and MSFT #1's one admitted T5 document was cited nowhere"
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md §8 item 12 — raising the ceiling is named as an operator decision
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/baseline/msft1/note.md:329-343 — the console's guidance table, and the judges' caveat that most rows rest on a third-party blog [S31]
items.recommendation: This is the operator's call, and it should be taken as a deliberate policy rather than drifted into. The cheapest honest answer is a two-step: (1) fetch the results-release exhibit (previous items), which gives a T1 document carrying whatever guidance the issuer put in writing — for AstraZeneca that is the guidance itself; for Microsoft it is the results release but not the call; and (2) wire the existing issuer-IR adapter for the operator-supplied domain only, which is what it was built for, so a results presentation or transcript enters as T2 and a section may cite it. Only then consider raising a named section's ceiling. What must not happen is the console's own weakest move: the judges noted its FY27 guidance rested on a licensing blog. A platform whose whole claim is traceability should print guidance only where an issuer stated it, and say so where it did not.
items.adrSubject: What counts as management guidance, which tiers may support it, and whether the issuer-IR adapter is wired into acquisition — a change to the evidence policy ADR 0023's spine set and to F-21's tier ceiling.
items.tests: tests/test_section_evidence.py::TestGuidanceNeedsAnIssuerStatement — a T2 issuer document in the pack reaches growth_outlook only when the section's ceiling admits it, and a T5 secondary never supports a guidance figure alone; tests/test_filings.py::TestTheIssuerDomainIsTheOperatorsNotDiscovered — a link off-domain is dropped before any fetch.
items.acceptance: A replayed AZN run carries the guidance sentence from its results 6-K, footnoted to a hashed T1 artefact. A replayed MSFT run either carries the written guidance from the results release or states plainly that the outlook was given on a call the run does not hold — not silence.

options.name: Written guidance only, from T1 filing exhibits
options.change: Rely on the results-release exhibit; no new source, no tier change.
options.cost: Comes free with the exhibit fetch.
options.risk: Microsoft-shaped filers give guidance verbally; the report says so and scores 'partly'. Honest, and still better than absent.

options.name: Wire the issuer-IR adapter for an operator-named domain
options.change: Call `discover_documents` during acquire with the domain the operator supplies; presentations and transcripts enter as T2; raise growth_outlook's ceiling to T2.
options.cost: A few sessions plus an ADR.
options.risk: First adapter whose candidate URLs come from untrusted content — the module was built with that in mind and the fetch layer enforces the allowlist, but it needs the ADR.

options.name: Raise the ceiling to T5 for named sections
options.change: Let secondary reporting support a guidance table, always labelled.
options.risk: Highest. Invariant 1 still holds (the page is hashed), but a figure whose only support is a blog is the console's weakest result, and adopting it trades away the platform's one unambiguous win.

items.challengeNote: The ceiling is not what blocks issuer material. `SourceTier` is ordered with T1 lowest and the check is `source.source_tier.rank <= policy.max_tier_rank` (evidence.py:634), so a max_tier of T4_LICENSED_MARKET **already admits T2**. Option B's "raise growth_outlook's ceiling to T2" is backwards — it would tighten the section, not loosen it. Nothing needs to move in the evidence policy to let a T2 issuer presentation reach growth_outlook; the single blocker is that no code path calls the adapter. That shortens option B materially (wire the caller, pass the operator's domain to the fetcher, no migration) and removes the migration from `filesTouched`. The ADR is still needed, but for the untrusted-URL question and for what counts as guidance, not for a tier change. The T4 ceiling only bites on T5 secondary reporting, which is option C and which the item already argues against.
items.invariantRisk: Invariant 8 is the live one for option B: the IR adapter is the first source whose candidate URLs come out of a page the issuer controls (src/aer/sources/issuer.py:1-30 sets out the three controls). The ADR must record that the domain is operator-supplied and never learned. Option C additionally collides with SourceTier's own rule that T5 is "never the sole support for a numeric claim" (src/aer/core/enums.py:180-188) — raising a ceiling does not repeal that, so a T5-only guidance table would be refused anyway.

items.title: The run holds eight named competitors with CIKs and rationales the operator personally confirmed, and prints none of them
items.problem: "Competitive position with named competitors" is scored absent by all three judges, who noted that the Industry section "names no company" and that the comps section says "every one of the eight proposed peers was excluded" without naming one. Yet MSFT #1's peer gate payload holds Alphabet, Amazon, Oracle, Salesforce, SAP, IBM, Adobe and Apple — each with a CIK resolved against the SEC registry and each with a one-sentence rationale of exactly the kind the checklist item asks for ("AWS competes directly with Azure in cloud infrastructure; Amazon's retail segment is not comparable"). The operator read those eight names and approved them at a gate. They then vanish.
items.rootCause: Two places, neither of them the model's fault. The comps narrative is written to count peers and never name them — `src/aer/calc/comps.py:380-415` composes "every one of the {n} proposed peers was excluded, because {reasons}" from counts and reason strings only. items.challengeNote: (a) "The footnote is the approval, not a fetched page" is not available. Only three citation kinds are constructed anywhere in src/ — calculation, source_document and assumption — and ADR 0074 states the rule as a schema fact: `SourceKind` gains no fifth value, `SourceRef` no fifth constructor, and the exclusive choice on `claims` has no column for a held view. An approval footnote is a new record kind and a new ADR, not a session. Name the peers with no footnote — which is what the comps sentence already does, since it is deterministic Python prose carrying no citation — and drop the footnote claim. (b) The acceptance is unreachable as written: two of the three doc-B judges scored the console's named competitors "present-unsourced", not "present-sourced", and the platform naming an operator-approved slate with no fetched support will land in the same place. Set the target at present-unsourced. Also position this against docs/plan/ROADMAP.md:1131-1163 (§4.15), which already rewrote this very sentence once and explicitly leaves "whether to keep buying the model's slate at all" as an undecided operator question — the item reads as a fresh find and is the next step of a recorded one.
items.invariantRisk: Invariant 1 is close but not breached: a peer's name and CIK are registry-resolved under ADR 0059 rather than asserted, and no figure is claimed. It *is* breached the moment the approval becomes a citation, because a confirmed gate payload is not a hashed external artefact and ADR 0074 forbids the shape.

items.title: The filing's own competition prose and its segment footnote are squeezed out of the excerpt budget, or out of scope entirely
items.problem: The platform's one unanimous checklist win is the filing's own risk factors, present and sourced on both platform reports and absent from both console notes. The same filing's Competition section, which names competitors by name, produces nothing. And the segment footnote — where the dollars are — is not read at all. In a 13,993-word MSFT report only five footnotes cite the 10-K, three of them belonging to the segment chart: the document quotes the filing repeatedly in prose ("the 10-K is explicit about the cause") without citing it.
items.rootCause: Two mechanisms. (a) Scope: `_PROSE_ITEMS["10-K"] = {ITEM1, ITEM1A, ITEM7}` (src/aer/services/filings.py:127-131). Item 8, Financial Statements and Supplementary Data, where the segment footnote and its dollar table live, is deliberately outside every 10-K's excerpt regions. (b) Budget: `MAX_EXCERPTS = 60` per document (filings.py:83) and `_score` is an unweighted count of 28 terms, of which "risk", "regulat", "litigation", "competition", "cost", "market share", "pricing", "demand" and "currency" are the everyday vocabulary of Item 1A — so a 25,000-word risk-factors item is structurally favoured over Item 1's Competition subsection. The report's own output is consistent with this: risk factors abundant, competition prose absent. I have not counted the scores over the stored artefact, so the second mechanism is a hypothesis; the first is certain from the code.

items.recommendation: Two deterministic changes. First, put the segment footnote in scope: add Item 8 to the 10-K regions (and the 20-F equivalent) with its own excerpt allowance, so the section that carries segments can quote the note that states them; this complements rather than replaces the structured segment rows, because the allocation policy a reader wants to know about is prose, not XBRL. Second, allocate the 60 excerpt slots per item rather than globally, so Item 1 and Item 7 each keep a reserved share and cannot be crowded out by Item 1A — the same reservation pattern the evidence pack already uses to stop listings starving excerpts. Rank the pool before truncating it at `_EXCERPT_POOL`, not after.

items.challengeNote: `_score` (filings.py:655-663) returns `sum(1 for term in _WORTH_READING if term in lowered)` — a count of *distinct* terms present in one paragraph-sized block, capped at 28, not a count of occurrences, so length confers no advantage on a block. And `ranked = sorted(candidates, key=lambda pair: (-_score(pair[1]), pair[0]))` (filings.py:532) breaks ties by ascending document position, which favours Item 1 because Item 1 precedes Item 1A in every 10-K. On ties — which will be the common case in a 0-28 integer space — the crowding runs the *opposite* way to the item's claim. The per-item reservation may still be worth having, but it should be justified by the offline scoring run the item's own open question proposes, not by an asserted structural bias. Keep mechanism (a); demote (b) to "measure first".
items.invariantRisk: None. Both halves are deterministic selection over a filed document. Note only that adding Item 8 widens what a section may quote from a statements-and-notes region whose numbers must still come from XBRL facts, never from the excerpt — `covered_figures` enforces that, so state it in the test.

items.title: 1,592 dimensioned tags were dropped on one run and nobody was told
items.problem: AZN #2's segment sweep saw 3,637 dimensioned facts, wrote 65, and could not map 1,592 tags. Those 1,592 are recorded in a step output field and reach no gate, no coverage notice and no page. The audit's headline unmapped figures (496 on MSFT, 322 on AZN, 852 on the bank) are the aggregate's, not the sweep's, so the operator's mental model of "what the platform could not read" is missing the entire dimensional half — and "no product-level revenue" may be sitting inside that number.
items.rootCause: Deliberate, and correct as far as it goes: `SegmentSweep.as_dict` names its keys `segment_unmapped_tags` etc. specifically so they do not merge into `unmapped_tags`, which feeds the confirmation gate (src/aer/services/segments.py:60-72, and ADR 0058: "a breakdown tagged with an invented element is counted in the step output rather than stopping the run"). The gap is that counting it in the step output was treated as sufficient. The gate is the wrong destination — stopping a run to ask about a breakdown would be worse — but the coverage notice and the run's diagnostics are the right ones, and the sweep reaches neither. There is also a silent second loss: multi-axis cells are skipped entirely (segments.py:161-163) and not even counted.

Keep them out of the gate, as ADR 0058 decided. This is the difference between a report that quietly lacks product-level revenue and one that tells its reader which tags would have produced it, which is the platform's whole proposition and the thing the console structurally cannot do.

items.title: A bank's revenue: the three options, costed against the code
items.problem: M&T reports no total-revenue caption after FY2023, so `revenue` resolves to `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` — $1,541m (FY2024) and $1,657m (FY2025) — against net income of $2,588m and $2,851m. Eleven relations are impossible, `figure_plausibility` scores 11 against a threshold of 0, and no bank can reach an approved report. Seven of the eleven are quarterly (Q1 FY2025, Q1 FY2026, Q2 FY2024/25/26, Q3 FY2024/25); two are annual income-above-revenue; two are the FY2024/FY2025 net margins of 1.679 and 1.721.
items.rootCause: `US_GAAP_ALIASES` maps three ASC 606 spellings onto `revenue` (src/aer/core/concepts.py:196-198). `REVENUE_TAG_PREFERENCE` (src/aer/core/concepts.py:348-360) correctly ranks a total above a component, and `_prefer_total_revenue` (src/aer/sources/sec/companyfacts.py:199-235) demotes the loser to its raw tag — but only where a total exists for the same period. Where none exists the component wins by default. Nothing sums `net_interest_income` (InterestIncomeExpenseNet, src/aer/core/concepts.py:206) and `noninterest_income` (NoninterestIncome, src/aer/core/concepts.py:208), because a sum is a calculation and no definition claims it: `_DERIVED_SUMS` (src/aer/calc/statements.py:358-363) admits only identities that hold for every filer in both GAAP and IFRS, and this one does not.
evidence: audit §8 item 2; F-24 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:867-901)
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/mtb/run-export.json — figure_plausibility value 11, all 11 failure strings

docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/mtb/truth.json — revenue FY2021-23 `us-gaap:Revenues` 5,992 / 8,179 / 9,643m; FY2024-25 `us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` 1,541 / 1,657m; net_interest_income FY2021-25 3,825 / 5,822 / 7,115 / 6,852 / 6,948m
src/aer/core/concepts.py:196-198,205-208,348-373
src/aer/sources/sec/companyfacts.py:199-235
src/aer/calc/statements.py:344-363,455-500
items.recommendation: Take **withhold first, then derive on top of it** — they are not exclusive, and the audit's framing of three mutually exclusive answers is what makes the choice look hard. Withholding is one edit at the parse layer and reaches every surface at once, because every surface reads `concept == "revenue"`; it clears all eleven findings and unblocks gate 2. Deriving then adds a traced total so a bank's report has a revenue and a margin, and the surfaces that read facts can be moved onto the derived figure deliberately rather than by accident. Do not take 'leave it': it is not actually safe (see `turnover-check-never-fires`) and it has a standing cost — the audit spent £9.64 on two M&T runs for no report. **Which definition of a bank's revenue to adopt remains the operator's, and it is the only part of this that is.**

options.name: A — Derive it
options.change: Add `bank_total_revenue` as a `@traced` sum in `src/aer/calc/statements.py` (beside `subtotal_sum` at :322-330), and a **separate, gated** derivation list in `assemble` (:455-500) — not `_DERIVED_SUMS`, whose stated rule is that every entry holds by definition for every filer. Give `assemble` a `profile: SectorProfile | None` argument (`aer.core.sectors` is core, so `aer.calc` may import it) and derive only when the profile is `banks` or `insurers` and `revenue` is absent for the period. Pass it at the one call site, `src/aer/services/analysis.py:280`; `analyse_company` already carries `profile` (:214, :242). Refuse the derivation when only one component is present — a partial sum labelled 'revenue' is the same failure again. **Then the five surfaces that read facts rather than calculations**, or the fix clears only 4 of 11 findings: `_figure_scenes` (src/aer/services/evaluations.py:599-657), `_latest_rows` and `_annual_series` (src/aer/render/glance.py:264,293), `_revenue_margin_input` (src/aer/services/exhibits.py:198) and the drafter's evidence pack (src/aer/sections/evidence.py:135). Quarterly periods have no derivation at all, because `analyse_company` builds annual statements only (src/aer/services/analysis.py:245-252, `annual_facts`).
options.cost: A few sessions. Six surfaces, a new argument threaded through a pure module, and a quarterly gap that has no derivation to offer.
options.risk: The definition must be right. If derived FY2021-23 does not reproduce the reported `Revenues` within rounding, the definition is wrong and the platform would be publishing a number no filer stated.

options.name: B — Withhold it
options.change: One edit in `src/aer/sources/sec/companyfacts.py`: extend `_prefer_total_revenue` (:199-235), or add a sibling `_demote_partial_revenue`, so a `RevenueFromContractWithCustomer*` fact is demoted to its raw tag when the same document reports, for the same period and unit, a revenue line outside ASC 606's scope that exceeds it — concretely `InterestIncomeExpenseNet`. The function already demotes by rewriting `concept` to `raw_concept`, so the fact stays stored, visible and hashed; it simply stops being 'revenue'. **This needs no sector gate, and that is the point**: `acquire` runs before `classify` and before the SECTOR_SPECIALIST gate (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:412-424), so a classification-conditional rule cannot be applied where facts are written. Then two consequences must be handled deliberately: `_latest_rows` (src/aer/render/glance.py:264) anchors the whole front page on the newest fact carrying `revenue` and would silently fall back to FY2023, showing a 2.5-year-old period's net income and EPS; and `_revenue_margin_input` (src/aer/services/exhibits.py:198) would draw a revenue history that stops in 2023 with no note. Move the now-meaningless bank ratios into `SECTOR_PROFILES['banks'].not_meaningful_ratios` (src/aer/core/sectors.py:172-180) so the reader is told 'not meaningful for a bank' rather than 'no fact for this concept'.
options.cost: A session for the parse rule and its tests; a second for the front-page anchor and the chart note.
options.risk: A bank's report carries no revenue and no margin at all. Honest, and thinner than a console note on the same brief — which is a direct cost against Issue 2.

options.name: C — Leave it
options.change: Nothing. `figure_plausibility` refuses the report at gate 2 and no wrong figure reaches a reader.
options.cost: Nil to build; £7-8 per bank run that produces nothing, and Issue 2 stays lost for the whole sector.
options.risk: Not as safe as it reads. The turnover-floor relation of the same guard has never fired (see `turnover-check-never-fires`), so the guard's coverage is two relations, not three — and the wrong revenue still reaches the *prose*, where the model rationalised it rather than refusing it (report.md:102: 'pre-tax income exceeded reported revenue for the period, a relationship that reflects the composition of a bank's income statement').

items.adrSubject: Two, one per option, and they say different kinds of thing. For B: 'An ASC 606 component is not a total where the filer reports a larger revenue line outside ASC 606's scope for the same period' — a statement about the taxonomy, which is why it can live at the parse layer and needs no classification. For A: 'A bank's revenue is net interest income plus non-interest income' — a modelling definition, joining ADR 0070 and ADR 0029, which must also state that a reported total always wins and that a single present component never derives.
items.tests: tests/test_sec_companyfacts.py — a bank fixture reporting an ASC 606 component and `InterestIncomeExpenseNet` for one period and no total: the component must not map to `revenue`, must survive under its raw tag, and a period that also carries `Revenues` must still resolve to the total (the existing gap-A62 case must not regress). tests/test_statements.py — derivation only under a bank/insurer profile, refused when one component is absent, never overwriting a stated total. tests/test_run_evaluations.py — a scene set built from bank-shaped rows scoring `figure_plausibility` 0.
items.acceptance: The decisive one is free and offline: **for FY2021, FY2022 and FY2023, where M&T did report `Revenues`, the derived figure must equal the reported one within rounding** — 5,992m, 8,179m and 9,643m against net interest income of 3,825m, 5,822m and 7,115m plus non-interest income for the same years, read from the archived companyfacts (sha256 31b7b199ea6bc258a238daac1215dbe0ad385cb801d7a08ec6c8bb93d57aa363, named in docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/mtb/truth.json). If the three years do not splice, the definition is wrong and nothing ships. Then: M&T FY2025 revenue 9,690m, net margin 0.294, asset turnover 0.0454, `figure_plausibility` 0 of 0, and gate 2 reachable. A live re-run at roughly £7.60 confirms it end to end, and should be spent only after the offline splice passes.
items.challengeNote: Two corrections, both strengthening. (1) The open question is closed: I read the archived companyfacts at var/artefacts/31/b7/31b7b199ea6bc258a238daac1215dbe0ad385cb801d7a08ec6c8bb93d57aa363 and the splice is exact, not approximate — FY2021 3,825 + 2,167 = 5,992 (reported `Revenues` 5,992); FY2022 5,822 + 2,357 = 8,179 (8,179); FY2023 7,115 + 2,528 = 9,643 (9,643). Delta zero in all three years. FY2024 derives 9,279m and FY2025 9,690m, and `Revenues` is genuinely absent for both. `RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense` is ABSENT from M&T's companyfacts entirely, which confirms that F-24's added alias cannot reach this filer. So Option A's definition is verified, its stated gating condition is met, and the ADR can cite three reproduced years rather than one data point. (2) The item under-labels its own conclusion: because `analyse_company` builds annual statements only (src/aer/services/analysis.py:246), Option A can never clear the seven quarterly findings and therefore can never on its own unblock gate 2. Option B is not the cheap alternative — it is the only one of the two that reaches gate 2, and the recommendation's 'withhold first, then derive' ordering is load-bearing rather than stylistic. State it that way or the operator will read the options as interchangeable.

items.title: A calculation-layer revenue fix reaches the ratio suite and nothing else
items.problem: The audit sizes the derivation as 'one function in aer.calc, one place in the ratio inputs that prefers it, and an ADR'. That would clear the two annual net-margin findings and, through the recomputed margins, two more — four of eleven. The seven quarterly income-above-revenue findings would stand, gate 2 would still refuse, the front page would still carry 'Revenue $442m' beside 'Net income $818m', the revenue-history chart would still draw 9,643 → 1,541 → 1,657, and the section writers would still be handed the fee-income fact labelled 'revenue' and still write prose about it.
items.rootCause: A derived revenue is a `Calculation`, not a `FinancialFact` — correctly, since invariant 3 distinguishes the two and a fact must be something a filer reported. But five of the six surfaces that show revenue read facts: `_figure_scenes` selects `FinancialFact.concept.in_(('revenue','net_income','total_assets'))` (src/aer/services/evaluations.py:612) across every fiscal period including quarters; `_latest_rows` anchors on the newest `revenue` fact (src/aer/render/glance.py:264) and `_annual_series` plots them (:293); `_revenue_margin_input` selects `FinancialFact.concept == 'revenue'` (src/aer/services/exhibits.py:198); `_INCOME_CONCEPTS` puts `revenue` first in the drafter's deterministic relevance order (src/aer/sections/evidence.py:134-135). Only `compute_ratios` (src/aer/calc/ratios.py:848-880), fed by `assemble`, reads the calculated line. And no quarterly statement is ever assembled: `analyse_company` reads `annual_facts` only (src/aer/services/analysis.py:245-252).

items.title: The plausibility guard's third relation has never run: it asks for a concept that does not exist
items.problem: `impossible_relations` holds three relations. Two fire. The third — revenue below one percent of assets on a billion-plus balance sheet — has never fired at gate 2 on any run, because the scene it is given always has `total_assets=None`. The M&T run recorded asset turnover of 0.00776 (FY2025, assets $213,510m) and 0.00740 (FY2024, assets $208,105m), both far below the 0.01 floor on a balance sheet 200× the $1bn threshold, and neither appears among the eleven findings. The module's own docstring cites that very run — 'the MTB run's mislabelled caption produced 0.0076' — as the calibration for the floor, and the run that produced it was never told.
items.rootCause: `_figure_scenes` selects `FinancialFact.concept.in_(('revenue','net_income','total_assets'))` and reads `held.get('total_assets')` (src/aer/services/evaluations.py:612,646). The canonical concept is `assets`: `US_GAAP_ALIASES` maps `Assets` → `assets` (src/aer/core/concepts.py:260) as does `IFRS_ALIASES` (:432), and `BALANCE_SHEET_LINES` carries `assets` (src/aer/calc/statements.py:110). No fact ever has concept `total_assets`, so the field is always None and the branch at src/aer/calc/plausibility.py:119-135 is unreachable from the gate. It survives because tests/test_plausibility.py exercises the pure function with `total_assets=` set by hand (lines 53, 88, 93, 112) and nothing tests the service that fills it.

It must fail against today's code. Add a companion assertion that every concept name `_figure_scenes` queries is a key of the canonical concept set, so the next renaming is caught by a test rather than by an audit.

items.challengeNote: Fully confirmed, and the strongest item in the set. `_figure_scenes` queries and reads the string `total_assets` (src/aer/services/evaluations.py:612, :646, :655) and `total_assets` appears nowhere else in src/ — the canonical concept is `assets` (`Assets` → `assets` at src/aer/core/concepts.py:260 and :432, `assets` in BALANCE_SHEET_LINES at src/aer/calc/statements.py:110). items.title: The sector gate's third answer, and where it has to be recorded
items.problem: The gate offers 'Approve and continue' and 'Reject and stop this run'. An operator looking at a classification they believe is wrong has nowhere to say so: approving grants a mandate over a label they disagree with, rejecting kills a run that has already been paid for. For M&T the classification was right, so it cost nothing; for a filer a bare SIC lookup mislabels, it is a gate with no right answer.
items.rootCause: The decision is coerced to a binary in the shared POST handler: `Decision.APPROVED if submitted.get('decision') == Decision.APPROVED.value else Decision.REJECTED` (src/aer/web/pages.py:1798-1802), fed by the two buttons in the template every gate shares (src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:118-123). Downstream, `confirmed_classification` reads only `Decision.APPROVED` (src/aer/services/sectors.py:208-214) and hashes the classify step's own output (:229-231), so there is no place for a payload the operator corrected. The schema is already ahead of the surface: `Decision.AMENDED` exists (src/aer/core/enums.py:169) and has a rendered word (src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:398), and is written nowhere in `src/`.
evidence: audit §8 item 4 and F-26 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:923-946, 1129-1139)

src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:118-123
src/aer/services/sectors.py:180-243
src/aer/core/enums.py:164-169; src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:395-399

items.recommendation: Take the narrow shape first and record the correction as a decision, not as a re-run. Add a third button on the sector gate only — override the decision block in `runs/sector.html` rather than widening `_gate.html`, so no other gate acquires a third answer by accident — offering a closed list of the seven other profiles plus 'no specialist sector', with a **mandatory** reason. Record `Decision.AMENDED` with the corrected payload and its own hash, and teach `confirmed_classification` to prefer the latest AMENDED over the classify step's proposal. The direction matters and must be handled explicitly: amending *towards* a profile that blocks a model is safe; amending *away* from one — 'this is not a bank' — unblocks `DCF_FCFF` and is exactly the permissive direction ADR 0029 is built around, so it needs the typed reason, the person recorded in `ValuationMandate.confirmed_by`, and the correction stated in the report's sector block. On F-26's second half — should the four non-blocking profiles stop a run once the third answer exists — the answer is no: keep F-23's narrowing permanently and record it in the same ADR, because a profile that blocks nothing changes only which warnings a report carries and does not need a person to confirm it.

options.name: Correct the classification
options.change: Third answer offering the other profiles and 'no specialist sector'; AMENDED carries the corrected payload; the mandate is minted from the amendment.
options.cost: A session for the surface and the service, a second for the report disclosure and tests.
options.risk: A person can now move a run to the permissive answer. Mitigated by the mandatory reason, the recorded actor and the report disclosure — and it is strictly better than today, where the same operator's only routes are to approve a label they disagree with or to bin the run.

options.name: Not this sector, standard model
options.change: A single extra answer that records the correction and falls through to the unclassified mandate, with no re-classification list.
options.cost: An hour or two less than the above.
options.risk: A REIT mislabelled as a bank ends up unclassified rather than a REIT, so the run loses the REIT's blocks and warnings. Cheaper and strictly worse.

options.name: Leave it at two
options.change: Nothing.
options.risk: Survivable only while `propose_from_sic` proposes nothing but blocking profiles. The day a non-blocking profile is proposed again, the gate has no right answer.

items.adrSubject: A classification may be corrected by the person who confirms it, and a correction towards the permissive answer is recorded with its reason and disclosed in the report.
items.tests: tests/test_sectors_service.py — `confirmed_classification` returns the amended profile, not the proposed one; an amendment whose payload hash does not match what was shown is refused exactly as an approval is; an amendment to 'no specialist sector' yields the unclassified mandate and the run's report carries the correction. tests/test_sectors_enforcement.py — a run amended away from `banks` may mint a `DCF_FCFF` mandate, and the mandate names the person who did it.
items.acceptance: On the fake scene, a run classified as `banks` and amended to 'no specialist sector' with a reason reaches the standard model, its report states the correction and who made it, and `aer.services.approvals` holds exactly one decision at the gate. A run amended from `early_stage_tech` to `banks` blocks the DCF.
items.challengeNote: The recommendation is right that amending away from a blocking profile is the permissive direction and needs the ADR — but it should also require that the amendment's own payload hash is recorded and re-checked at the deep guard, because `confirmed_classification` currently derives `expected` from the classify step's output alone (:229-231). If an AMENDED approval simply becomes preferred without changing what `expected` is computed over, the hash check either fails every amended run or has to be skipped for them — the second is a silent hole in exactly the permissive path the ADR exists to fence.
items.invariantRisk: ADR 0029 (the sector block is a type, not a check) — amending away from `banks` mints a `DCF_FCFF` mandate that ADR 0029's acceptance criterion says a bank ticker cannot reach by any route. The item flags adrNeeded correctly; the new ADR must be written as an amendment to 0029, not merely alongside it.

items.title: The document the operator approves at the final gate is not the document that would be rendered
items.problem: The final-gate review page assembles a document missing the sector block, the comparables disclosure and the back-of-document exhibits pack. For a bank that block is the whole of the disclosure: it is where the reader is told the discounted cash flow was refused rather than merely absent, where the two bank warnings appear, and where the five required bank metrics the run did not produce are named. M&T's document carries none of it. The docstring above the call says 'The document as it will be… Approving a bullet list and receiving a report is not a review; the operator decides on the thing itself' — and it is demonstrably not the thing itself.
items.rootCause: `src/aer/web/pages.py:1103` calls `render_markdown(session, job=job, request=research_request, company=company)` with no `sector`, `comps`, `charts` or `style`. In the same module, `_run_document` (src/aer/web/pages.py:1416-1447) passes all four, and so does the render step (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3718-3731). `serialise_markdown` emits `_sector_block`, `_comps_block` and `_exhibits_block` only when those arguments arrive (src/aer/render/markdown.py:106-141, 186-214). A third caller, `assemble_document(context.session, job=job, request=request)` at src/aer/services/evaluations.py:187, is bare as well — so `presentation_integrity` has never scanned a sector block, a comps paragraph or an exhibits pack either.

Do the same at src/aer/services/evaluations.py:187, so the check that judges presentation judges the document a reader gets. Then add a test that asserts every caller of `assemble_document`/`render_markdown` in `src/` supplies the same argument set, because this is a defect of omission and omission is what a signature with four optional keyword arguments invites.

A regression test asserting the review page's markdown is byte-identical to the render step's for the same job state. tests/test_run_evaluations.py — `presentation_integrity` measured over a document that includes the sector and comps blocks.

Re-scope to: two call sites omit arguments a third supplies, `presentation_integrity` measures a document no reader receives, and a test should assert every `assemble_document`/`render_markdown` caller in src/ passes the same set. Remove `charts` from the claimed consequence and open it as its own finding — the back-of-document exhibits pack is empty on every run, including approved ones, which is a defect in `exportable_charts_for` or in how section-level charts are attached, and nobody has looked at it. Rewrite the acceptance as what it can actually be: reproduce the review page against mtb's stored record and diff it against `_run_document`'s serialisation for the same job state — that is measurable today and settles the provenance question at the same time.

items.title: Once the at-a-glance block is un-withheld, a bank's front page still has no bank figures in it
items.problem: Fixing revenue lets the at-a-glance block render. What it renders for a bank is: Revenue, Net income, EPS, and headline calculations chosen for a discounted cash flow — gross margin, operating margin, net margin, free cash flow, net debt, WACC and value per share. For M&T, gross margin, operating margin, net debt and the two valuation rows are absent (a bank has no operating income line by its own profile, and the run recorded `cost_of_equity` and `residual_income_per_share`, never `wacc` or `value_per_share`). Free cash flow is present and is the one figure the bank profile's own warning says is not meaningful for a bank. The reader's first screen would carry a fee-income-shaped income statement and no appraisal.
items.rootCause: `_LATEST_CONCEPTS` (src/aer/render/glance.py:89-94) and `_HEADLINE_CALCULATIONS` (:99-110) are fixed tuples written for the standard model. Neither consults the confirmed sector. `INCOME_STATEMENT_LINES` already puts `interest_and_dividend_income`, `net_interest_income`, `provision_for_credit_losses` and `noninterest_income` where a bank's statement puts them (src/aer/calc/statements.py:75-82), so the concepts exist and the front page does not ask for them.

items.recommendation: Make both tuples sector-aware by reading the confirmed profile, the way `compute_ratios` already reads `not_meaningful_ratios`. For a bank: latest figures become net interest income, non-interest income, net income and EPS; headline calculations become cost of equity, return on equity, value per share (fade), premium to book and tangible book value per share, with free cash flow suppressed. Keep the shape declarative — two mappings keyed by sector key with the current tuples as the default — rather than a branch, so adding insurers and REITs later is a row.
items.tests: tests/test_glance (or the render tests) — a bank job whose recorded calculations include `residual_income_per_share` and `cost_of_equity` renders a headline table containing them and not `free_cash_flow`; an unclassified job renders exactly what it renders today.
items.acceptance: M&T's front page, re-assembled from its own record with revenue fixed, shows net interest income $6,948m, non-interest income $2,742m, net income $2,851m, cost of equity 9.33% and a value per share — and no free cash flow.
items.challengeNote: Two fixes to the acceptance and one design note. The acceptance asks for 'a value per share' — no calculation of that name exists on this run; the recorded name is `residual_income_per_share`, so the sector-keyed mapping must name that string or the test cannot pass. And reading the confirmed profile from `aer.render.glance` means the render layer importing `aer.services.sectors` for an async DB read; prefer threading the already-resolved profile down from `assemble_document`'s caller, which both `_run_document` and the render step already compute via `sector_note_for`, rather than adding a render→services dependency.

items.title: The appraisal's book value includes preferred capital and its share count is nine percent stale — both against figures the same document prints
items.problem: The residual-income valuation divides a total-equity value by a common-share count, and the two come from different dates. Book value is total stockholders' equity at 31 December 2025 — $29,177m — which includes M&T's preferred stock; the value is then divided by 158,791,000, the FY2025 diluted weighted average. The same report states 146.8 million diluted shares for the June 2026 quarter and 144,416,262 shares outstanding at 31 July 2026. So the published $184.47 and $186.53 per share are computed on a denominator 8-10% above the shares actually in issue, over a numerator that credits common holders with capital that belongs to preferred holders. Neither convention is stated anywhere in the document.
items.rootCause: `_inputs_from` takes `opening_book_value=required_line(latest, 'equity')` (src/aer/services/residual_income_run.py:579) — the `equity` concept, which maps `StockholdersEquity` (src/aer/core/concepts.py:279), a figure inclusive of preferred. `shares_outstanding=share_count(latest)` (:587) resolves through `share_count` (src/aer/services/valuation_run.py:450-469), which prefers `diluted_shares_outstanding` — a weighted average over the fiscal year, not a count at the balance-sheet date. There is no `preferred_stock` concept in the map at all, so the carrying amount cannot be subtracted even if the model wanted to.
evidence: audit §8 item 8 and F-21 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:1147-1150 and the F-21 bullet on modelling definitions), which records the definition as 'untested live… neither preferred stock nor non-controlling interests is mapped for M&T at all'
