items.title: A stale approval strands the run for ever, and the assumptions surface is the open door into it
items.problem: The operator approves a gate, then changes something the gate hashed — most commonly amends an assumption from the request's own assumptions page. The run resumes, finds the approval's hash no longer matches, and pauses saying "The page it was taken from has moved since. Open the review page again and decide on what it shows now." The operator opens the gate page and it says "Approved by you on 11 September 2026. A decision is not a state to re-assert; changing it needs a new run," with no form and only a "Back to the run" link. The two messages contradict each other and there is no third page. £7 of research is stranded.
items.rootCause: Two rules meet with nothing between them. `approvals.record_decision` refuses any second decision at a decided gate (src/aer/services/approvals.py:175-194) and `runs/_gate.html:71-78` therefore renders no form once `decided` is set — deliberately, per its own comment. Meanwhile `_require_approval` raises StepPaused with advice to decide again (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2178-2186). The open door is the per-request assumptions surface: `assumptions_page` (src/aer/web/routes.py:924-978) and `amend_assumption_page` (src/aer/web/routes.py:1132-1205) render and accept amendments with no awareness of any run or gate state, while the equivalent guard for the final gate — `gates.refuse_settling_after_decision` (src/aer/services/gates.py:63-80) — exists and is applied only on the settle path (src/aer/web/pages.py:1618-1624). The gate pages for themes and peers already hide their add-forms once decided (runs/themes.html:50, runs/peers.html:92); the assumptions list page does not.
evidence: Audit F-16 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:692-704) and §8 item 5 (:1148-1150)
src/aer/services/approvals.py:175-194 — `_refuse_if_already_decided`
src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:14-15, 71-78 — "A decided gate renders no form"
src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2178-2186 — the pause message telling the operator to decide again
src/aer/web/routes.py:1132-1205 — amend has no decided-gate guard; src/aer/web/routes.py:924-978 — the page that offers it
src/aer/services/gates.py:63-80 — the guard that exists, for the final gate only
src/aer/core/enums.py:164-169 and migrations/versions/0001_core_schema.py:70 — `Decision.AMENDED` already exists in the enum and in the native Postgres type, and nothing in src/ writes it
src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:398 — the interface already has a label for it
items.recommendation: Do both halves. Close the door first (an hour): refuse an amend or create against a request whose ASSUMPTIONS gate is decided, reusing the shape of `refuse_settling_after_decision`, and hide the forms on the list page the same way the theme and peer pages do. Then open the exit (a session): a superseding decision recorded as `Decision.AMENDED` against the live payload, admitted only when the recorded approval matches neither the seal nor the live page — which is exactly the state that has no way out today. The enum value, the Postgres type and the interface label are already there, so this is a rule and a form, not a migration. It changes the approvals model and so needs its own ADR beside it.
items.adrSubject: A decision may be superseded exactly when the payload it was taken on no longer exists, and the superseding decision is recorded as AMENDED beside the original rather than replacing it.
items.tests: `tests/test_approvals.py::a_decision_may_be_superseded_only_when_the_payload_has_moved` — record an approval, change the payload, assert a second APPROVED is still refused and an AMENDED against the live hash is accepted and releases the gate; and `tests/test_assumptions_web.py::amending_after_the_gate_is_decided_is_refused` — assert the amend route answers 409 and the list page renders no amend form. Both must fail on the current tree.
items.acceptance: On a live or fixtured run: approve the assumptions gate, amend a value, and reach an approved report without touching a terminal — or be refused the amend with a message that names the gate and the remedy. No run in the suite reaches AWAITING_APPROVAL with a decided gate and no available action.
items.challengeNote: One consequence the item does not carry into its ADR subject: a superseding decision recorded against the *live* payload will not, on its own, release the FINAL gate, because expected_hash there comes from the frozen seal step. Recording AMENDED against the live page puts the run in the other branch of vertical_slice_v1.py:2170-2184 — 'live == approval.payload_hash' — whose message names `aer reseal <job-id>`. The ADR must therefore say what a superseding decision does to the seal, and the item's delivery depends on the re-seal-from-the-page action listed under terminal-still-required, not only on a new form.

items.title: A run refused at gate 2 can be re-measured nowhere, and cannot even be superseded
items.problem: MSFT #2 reached gate 2 with ten of eleven checks green and `presentation_integrity` failing on twenty-one leaked UUIDs. The honest operator refuses. The fix then lands — and there is no way to ask the run to score itself again. Worse, pressing "Start run" on the same request returns the operator to the same dead console, because a rejected gate leaves the job AWAITING_APPROVAL, which is not a terminal state, so the run cannot be superseded. The only way forward is to cancel a run that has already stopped, which nothing says, and pay £7 again.
items.rootCause: Three facts compose. The eight evaluation rows are written once, inside the `validate` step (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:1658-1707). The engine skips any step whose row says SUCCEEDED (src/aer/workflow/engine.py:518-527), and nothing in `src/` invalidates a completed step row, so `validate` can never run again on that job. And a gate rejection raises StepPaused, which the engine records as AWAITING_APPROVAL (src/aer/workflow/engine.py:747-758) — a state excluded from TERMINAL_JOB_STATUSES (src/aer/core/enums.py:115-117) — so `runs._may_be_superseded` (src/aer/services/runs.py:165-172) returns False and `start_run` hands back the existing dead job (src/aer/services/runs.py:92-94).
evidence: Audit F-22 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:793-829): "there is no way to re-measure the check after a fix … the metrics are written at validate, the run waits at gate 2 for ever, and no CLI command or page re-evaluates a job"
Audit §4.3 use case 2 (:378) and §9 (:1200-1203): "That £6.80 run stays unapproved, because nothing re-evaluates a finished job"
Audit §8 item 10 (:1145-1147) — "what re-runs after a late change?"
src/aer/workflow/engine.py:518-527 (skip-what-succeeded), :747-758 (StepPaused → AWAITING_APPROVAL)
src/aer/core/enums.py:101-117 — AWAITING_APPROVAL is explicitly not terminal
src/aer/services/runs.py:77-115, :165-172 — supersede requires terminal and no report
items.recommendation: Add a single re-measure action on the gate-2 page and the console — "Score this run again" — that invalidates the `validate` step row for this job, appends an audit event saying who asked and why, and re-enqueues. `validate` is already idempotent in effect (it overwrites the evaluation rows and refills the deterministic sections) and costs a fraction of a run; the red-team and revise steps stay untouched, so the sealed payload does not move unless the document actually changed. Separately, and independently useful, make a rejected gate reachable for supersede: either treat a run with a REJECTED gate decision as superseding-eligible in `_may_be_superseded`, or offer "Start again from this request" on the console with the cancel-then-start it implies made explicit. The first half is a new capability and needs an ADR (what may re-run after a late change, and what that does to the audit record); the second is a bug fix.
items.adrSubject: A completed scoring step may be invalidated and re-run on the operator's recorded request; the earlier scores keep their rows and the audit chain records who asked.
items.tests: `tests/test_run_api.py::TestARefusedCheckCanBeScoredAgain` — a job whose `validate` recorded a failure is re-scored after the underlying rows change, the new evaluation rows replace the old on the job, the prior rows survive as history, and the audit chain gains the event; plus `tests/test_runs_service.py::a_run_rejected_at_a_gate_can_be_started_again`. Both fail today.
items.acceptance: Re-run the MSFT #2 job (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft2/) from its own record under the current tree: `presentation_integrity` re-measures to 0 failures on the live job, not only on a re-assembled document, and the run can then be approved. That is exactly what audit §9 records as not established.
items.challengeNote: Re-scope: the item is 'a re-measure action plus a re-seal action plus a superseding decision', and it depends on terminal-still-required as well as stale-approval-dead-end. Drop the claim about eight rows (it is eleven). The test and the ADR subject as drafted ('the prior rows survive as history', 'the earlier scores keep their rows') contradict an existing recorded contract: evaluations.evaluate_run's docstring (services/evaluations.py:143-145) states that a re-validation *replaces* the rows because 'the run's citation score must be one answer, not a history', and _write executes DELETE FROM evaluations for the job (services/evaluations.py:862). Keeping history needs either a new table or a decision to reverse that rule — say which in the ADR, or change the test to assert replacement. Effort: 'a session' is right for the re-enqueue half only; with the seal and the superseding decision it is two to three sessions.
items.invariantRisk: No CLAUDE.md invariant is breached (the re-run is deterministic code re-measuring stored rows), but the drafted ADR subject would overturn evaluations.evaluate_run's documented replace-not-append rule, which is a recorded design decision in code rather than in docs/adr/.

items.title: A run whose gate was rejected keeps saying "Waiting for you" and links to a page with no decision on it
items.problem: After rejecting at any gate the console renders a red panel headed "Waiting for you — Nothing further happens, and nothing further is spent, until you approve or reject it", with a primary button to the gate page. The gate page says "DECIDED — Rejected by you on …" and offers "Back to the run". The operator can bounce between the two indefinitely. Nothing anywhere says the run is over.
items.rootCause: `approvals.pending_gate` answers from the paused step's recorded gate name and never consults the approvals table (src/aer/services/approvals.py:245-254), so a gate that has been decided is still reported as pending. The console template keys its entire "Waiting for you" block on `awaiting` (job.status is AWAITING_APPROVAL) and its buttons on `pending_gate` (src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:64-108), neither of which can tell an undecided gate from a decided one.
evidence: src/aer/services/approvals.py:233-264 — `pending_gate` reads the paused step, then falls back to gate order; no decision is consulted on the first path
src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:64-108 — the panel and the gate buttons
src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:71-78 — the decided panel the buttons lead to
src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2157-2161 — a rejected gate pauses with "The run stops here", which nothing surfaces as a state
src/aer/core/enums.py:115-117 — the job stays non-terminal, so the console's `awaiting` branch keeps firing
items.recommendation: Make `pending_gate` return None when the named gate already carries a decision, and give the console a third state for "this run was stopped by your decision at gate X on date" with the two things actually available: read what was produced, or start again. This is the smallest possible change and it closes the visible half of both dead ends above even before either is fixed.
items.tests: `tests/test_web_console.py::a_rejected_gate_is_not_reported_as_pending` — a job with a REJECTED approval at the paused gate renders no "Waiting for you" panel and no gate button, and says which decision stopped it. Fails today.
items.acceptance: Reject at gate 2 on a fixtured run and the console names the decision, the date and the two next steps; no path leads back to a page with no form on it.
items.challengeNote: Scope and effort are understated. pending_gate has six callers, not one: src/aer/web/pages.py:235, src/aer/web/gates.py:219 (the shared gate frame's journey, which uses it to mark 'current'), src/aer/web/overview/research.py:57 and overview/research_pages.py:68 (the 'what needs you' surfaces and ADR 0089's /runs/active), and src/aer/api/routes/runs.py:378 (the JSON contract). Changing its semantics changes what the API returns, so filesTouched must add those four files and the API's tests, and 'an hour' is better read as half a session. Also soften the problem statement: the console is not silent — it already offers 'Cancel this run' on the same page (console.html:395-415).

items.title: The unmapped-concepts gate asks one question over hundreds of rows and offers no way to answer it in parts
items.problem: The gate asks "does this gap matter?" and then shows every tag the concept map could not place: 496 rows on Microsoft, 312 on AstraZeneca and 852 on M&T, with the largest figure each held and its share of the biggest mapped line. The page is 7,911 words on MSFT #2 and 13,592 on the bank. There is one approve button and one reject button for the lot. An operator cannot mark a row as read, record that a particular extension matters, ask for it to be mapped, or approve "everything under a tenth of a per cent" — so in practice the honest reading is impossible and the gate is cleared on faith.
items.rootCause: `_unmapped_rows` emits one row per unplaced tag with no grouping and no threshold (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:1127-1180); `unmapped_gate_payload` carries the whole list (:1221-1242); and `unmapped_gate_required` fires on any non-empty list at all (:1244-1257). The template renders every row and offers only a client-side filter box (src/aer/web/templates/runs/financials.html:30-93). The decision surface is the shared two-button frame (src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:118-123), so the only vocabulary available is approve-all or reject-all.
evidence: Audit §4.2 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:356): "the unmapped-concepts page carried 105 items on MSFT, 51 on AZN and 304 on the bank"

Run exports, primary: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/gate-UNMAPPED_CONCEPTS.json `payload.unmapped_concepts` = 496 rows; azn2 = 312; mtb = 852. 205, 145 and 538 of those are ≥1% of the biggest mapped line
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft2/screens/financials.json — 7,911 words; mtb — 13,592 words
src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:1127-1180, :1221-1257
src/aer/web/templates/runs/financials.html:30-113

HYPOTHESIS: I could not reconcile the audit's 105/51/304 with any count derivable from the exports (distinct labels, rows with a figure, share thresholds, taxonomy splits all give different numbers). Either measure puts the page in the hundreds of rows; the discrepancy is worth settling before quoting a figure back to the operator.
items.recommendation: Do not remove rows — the evidence must stay complete. Split the question instead. Lead with the rows that could change an answer (a materiality band the payload already has the share for), collapse the rest behind one disclosure with its own count, and let the operator mark an individual tag for the concept map's curation queue — §2.8 of the roadmap already built the curation mechanism (`aer curation-worksheet`), so this is a door onto work that exists. The gate's approval stays one decision over the whole set, which keeps ADR-level semantics unchanged. Materially the question is whether the gate should fire at all when every unplaced tag is below a stated share of the biggest mapped line; that is a change to what a run stops for, and it is the operator's.
items.adrSubject: When an extraction's unplaced tags all fall below a stated share of the filer's largest mapped line, the run records the fact and does not stop a person to confirm it.
items.tests: `tests/test_web_gates.py::the_unmapped_gate_leads_with_what_could_change_the_answer` — a payload of 400 rows of which six exceed the band renders six rows above the fold and 394 behind one disclosure, with both counts stated, and the approved payload hash still covers all 400. Fails today.
items.acceptance: On the MSFT #1 payload the page's first screen carries fewer than twenty rows and names how many are behind the disclosure; the approved hash is byte-identical to today's for the same rows.
items.challengeNote: Two details. The page is longer than the item says: financials.html also renders payload.refused_concepts below the unmapped table (financials.html:115+), which any materiality-banding design has to account for. And filesTouched names src/aer/services/concepts.py, which does not exist — the curation mechanism lives in src/aer/services/curation.py and the concept map in src/aer/core/concepts.py.
items.invariantRisk: None, provided the approved payload still hashes all rows as the item says. Note only that unmapped_gate_required's docstring (vertical_slice_v1.py:1244-1257) mirrors IxbrlExtraction.needs_confirmation, so a share-threshold suppression has to change both or they will disagree about whether a run needs confirmation.

items.title: The assumptions gate makes the operator source a risk-free rate and an equity risk premium by hand on every run, while a complete macro stack sits unwired
items.problem: Every run stops and asks the operator to type values the platform could fetch or remember. On MSFT the gate named two outstanding: risk_free_rate ("No macroeconomic series has been acquired for this run … Enter the rate you are using and say which instrument and date it is from") and equity_risk_premium. On AZN #2 it named four, adding tax_rate and beta; on the bank, three. Each needs a value, a unit and a written justification the service refuses to do without. Nothing carries an answer forward from the last run, so the same two values are researched, typed and justified every £7 report — and a hand-typed rate is the one number in the valuation with no source behind it, which is precisely what the sceptic judge attacks.
items.rootCause: The macro acquisition path is fully built and has no caller. `MacroClient` (src/aer/sources/macro/client.py:111) is never constructed anywhere in `src/`; `macro.record_series` (src/aer/services/macro.py:81), the only writer of `MacroObservationRow`, has no caller in `src/`; `macro.risk_free_rate_as_at` (:173) has no caller in `src/`. `runtime.RuntimeServices.for_execution` lists five services and no macro client (src/aer/runtime.py:64-80) — the same omission its own docstring says lost the price client. So `macro_observations` is empty on every run and the gate's reason string (src/aer/services/assumption_gate.py:210) is literally true. The equity risk premium has no source by design and no place to store a standing one: assumptions are per-request rows only, with no defaults surface. Every proposal must carry a justification (`_require_justification`, src/aer/services/assumptions.py:355-358), and `confirm-all` deliberately skips rows with no value (src/aer/web/routes.py:1112-1125), so an outstanding name can only be cleared by typing.
evidence: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/gate-ASSUMPTIONS.json `payload.outstanding` — risk_free_rate, equity_risk_premium; azn2 — tax_rate, risk_free_rate, beta, equity_risk_premium; mtb — risk_free_rate, beta, equity_risk_premium
Audit §4.2 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:357): "2 on MSFT, 5 on AZN, 3 on the bank — each with a justification the page requires"; §4.4 check 5 (:396)
src/aer/sources/macro/client.py:111 — MacroClient, no constructor call in src/
src/aer/services/macro.py:81 (record_series) and :173 (risk_free_rate_as_at) — neither called from src/
src/aer/runtime.py:64-80 — the execution service list, macro absent
src/aer/sources/macro/series.py:382-389 — `RISK_FREE_SERIES = {"USD": "us_treasury_10y"}`, licence-cleared in the module docstring; no GBP entry, settled by ADR 0026
src/aer/services/assumption_gate.py:210 — the reason the gate gives
src/aer/services/assumptions.py:355-358 — a justification is mandatory
items.recommendation: Two changes, in order. First, wire the macro client into the run: build it in `runtime`, add it to `for_execution`, and add an acquisition step before `propose_assumptions` that records the currency's risk-free series through `record_series` and proposes the rate as a *derived* assumption carrying its series key, observation date and vintage — `as_rate` already does the percentage conversion through a traced calculation. This removes one hand-typed value per USD run and converts the discount rate's largest input from an operator opinion into a sourced, dated fact with a lineage node the claims page can already walk. A sterling filer still asks, and the refusal already names why. Second, give the equity risk premium (and any other name with no series) a standing operator value held in settings, proposed into each run with its stored justification and date and still confirmed at the gate — the operator agrees to it each time, so nothing about ADR 0046 weakens. Both are additive within the existing invariants: code acquires and proposes, a person confirms.
items.adrSubject: A standing operator assumption is a stored proposal with its own justification and date; it is re-proposed into every run and confirmed at the gate like any other, and never confirmed in advance.
items.tests: `tests/test_assumption_gate.py::the_risk_free_rate_comes_from_the_acquired_series` — a run whose macro step recorded us_treasury_10y proposes risk_free_rate with a `macro_observation` source and lists nothing outstanding for it; `tests/test_macro_acquisition.py` replays the FRED fixture through respx and asserts the vintage filter honours the as-of date. Both fail today because nothing constructs the client.
items.acceptance: A fresh USD run reaches the assumptions gate with at most one outstanding name (the equity risk premium, or none once the standing value exists), and the WACC footnote in the exported report resolves to a dated published series rather than to a number somebody typed.
items.challengeNote: Cite ADR 0082 and ADR 0084, which the item misses and which bear directly on both halves. ADR 0082 ('a rate is a dated observation with a source, not a number in a column') already decides the acquisition shape and states the rule that a rate a person typed is an attestation rather than a row in the rate store; ADR 0084 amends its source column. The first half may therefore be implementing an accepted decision rather than needing a new one — check 0082's Decision section before drafting. Keep the new ADR for the standing-value half only.
items.invariantRisk: The standing equity risk premium must not be stored as a macro observation: ADR 0082 reserves that table for sourced, dated published observations, and CLAUDE.md invariant 3 with ADR 0073 means a figure graded as an attestation propagates into a type with no field for it, so a DCF resting on one would reach no shareable surface. Holding it in settings and re-proposing it as an ordinary Assumption row with its justification, as the item describes, stays clear of that — but the ADR must say so explicitly, or the first implementer will reach for macro_observations.

items.title: The gate message promises a per-citation override that exists on no page and no command
items.problem: When a citation fails verification the run pauses at gate 2 and tells the operator: "Each can be overridden individually with a written reason, which is recorded; there is no way to wave all of them through at once." There is no such control. An unverified citation at the final gate therefore has no recovery at all — the run cannot proceed, and the message has sent the operator looking for a button that was never built.
items.rootCause: `override_citation` is implemented, tested and exported (src/aer/services/citations.py:185-225) and has no caller anywhere in `src/` — only `tests/test_citations.py` and `tests/test_provenance_surfaces.py` reach it. The promise is in `EvidenceReview.as_message` (src/aer/services/citations.py:60-70), raised by `_refuse_unsupported_evidence` (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2087-2122). The claim detail template can already *display* an override (src/aer/web/templates/claims/detail.html:143-145); nothing can create one.
evidence: Audit F-21 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:786-788) and §8 item 11 (:1157-1159)
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/code-audit-verification.md:72 — confirmed by grep in the audit's own verification pass
src/aer/services/citations.py:60-70 (the promise), :185-225 (the unreachable function)
src/aer/web/templates/claims/detail.html:143-145 — the display half exists
ADR 0018 §"An override is not a verification" (docs/adr/0018-only-code-confirms-a-citation.md:67-76) — the decision already anticipates this control and forbids a bulk one
items.recommendation: Build the surface ADR 0018 already describes: on the claim's evidence page, one override form per unverified citation, reason mandatory, no bulk action, the override visible in the report's own record and never collapsed into `excerpt_verified`. This needs no ADR — 0018 decided it, including that there is no bulk override — it needs a route and a form. If the operator would rather the promise be withdrawn than the control built, deleting the sentence from `as_message` is the alternative, and it is worse: an unverified citation then has no recovery and the run is simply lost.
items.tests: `tests/test_provenance_surfaces.py::an_unverified_citation_can_be_overridden_from_the_page` — post a reason, assert the row records reason, actor and time, that `excerpt_verified` is untouched, that `review_evidence` now counts it as overridden rather than unverified, and that a blank reason is refused. The service half already passes; the route half fails today.
items.acceptance: A run paused on an unverified citation reaches gate 2 through the interface alone, and the report it produces names the override and its reason where the citation is cited.
items.challengeNote: override_citation is defined at src/aer/services/citations.py:185-225 and appears nowhere else in src/ — the only importers are tests/test_citations.py and tests/test_provenance_surfaces.py. The promise is in EvidenceReview.as_message (citations.py:57-71), word for word as quoted. claims/detail.html:143-147 displays an override and nothing creates one. ADR 0018's section 'An override is not a verification' (docs/adr/0018-only-code-confirms-a-citation.md:66-79) decides the control, forbids a bulk one and requires the reason, so adrNeeded=false is right.

items.title: The terminal is still load-bearing, and the console says so out loud
items.problem: The product tells the operator, on the run console, "Past about ten minutes on one step, look at the terminal running `just worker` — that is where this run is actually happening, and where a failure appears first." A gate pause message tells them to run `aer reseal <job-id>`. Creating an account at all requires `aer seed-user`. The two commands that substantiate the platform's central claim — `aer verify-artefacts` and `aer verify-audit`, which walked 559 artefacts and 36 audit events in the audit — have no web surface at all. Nor do `aer export-run`, `aer diagnose`, `aer preflight`, `aer step`, `aer acceptance` or `aer backup`.
items.rootCause: There is one CLI and a partial web mirror of it, with no rule about which capabilities must exist on both. Of the twenty-eight commands in src/aer/cli.py, only replay (POST /runs/{job_id}/replay, src/aer/web/pages.py:1451) and the Obsidian export (:2913) have web equivalents; `reseal_final_gate` is reachable from the web only as a side effect of settling a disagreement (src/aer/web/pages.py:1618-1624), never as an operator action, while `aer reseal` (src/aer/cli.py:1419-1468) is what the pause message names.
evidence: src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:383-387 — the sentence naming the terminal
src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2178-2183 — "`aer reseal <job-id>`" inside a user-facing message
src/aer/web/pages.py:376-381 — "Nothing runs until one is started: `just worker`"
src/aer/web/templates/settings/index.html:73 — backup described as `aer backup`
Audit §4.2 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:358): "Anything that needed the terminal — yes"; §3.1 (:157-160) records verify-artefacts and verify-audit as the integrity proof
grep over src/aer/web/ finds no reference to verify_artefacts, verify_audit, preflight, diagnose, export_run or seed_user
items.recommendation: Pick the four that are journey-blocking and give each a page, in this order: (1) a *Check this platform's record* page running verify-artefacts and verify-audit and showing what they walked — this is the platform's differentiator and it currently lives only in a terminal; (2) a re-seal action on the gate page for the exact state its own message describes, which removes the last CLI reference from user-facing prose; (3) a preflight panel on the run-start page so a run is never commissioned into a dead worker, missing key or exhausted monthly cap; (4) the run export as a download beside the report. Starting Postgres, Redis and the worker is a separate question — a supervised worker subprocess or a single launcher is the answer there, and it is the operator's call whether that is worth a session.
items.tests: `tests/test_web_integrity.py::the_record_can_be_verified_from_the_interface` — the page reports the same artefact and audit counts the CLI does over the same fixture database; `tests/test_web_gates.py::a_drifted_seal_can_be_resealed_from_the_page` — the gate that today names `aer reseal` offers the action and the message no longer names a command. Both fail today.
items.acceptance: A grep of every user-facing template and every StepPaused message finds no shell command. An operator can verify the artefact store and the audit chain from the browser.
items.challengeNote: Effort is the weak part. 'A few sessions' covers four pages only if the verification page is a page; `aer verify-artefacts` re-read and re-hashed 559 artefacts in the audit (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:139-141, not :157-160 as cited), which is a background job with a progress surface rather than a request handler — budget that page separately. Add the dependency the diagnosis omits: the re-seal action here is a prerequisite for refused-check-no-remeasure, because re-scoring moves the live payload off the frozen seal.

items.title: 135 code identifiers on the gate pages, and metric names and twelve-place decimals in the exported document
items.problem: The pages an operator decides on, and the document a reader is handed, both speak in code. The gate screens carry 135 distinct machine identifiers — `gate_unmapped_concepts`, `balance_sheet_liquidity`, `capex_intensity`, `dcf_fcff`, `value_per_share_gordon_growth`. The bank's front-page coverage notice reads "the figure_plausibility, presentation_integrity validation checks failed" and then "net income 818000000.000000 exceeds revenue 442000000.000000". The validation appendix prints scores as `0E-8` and `1.00000000`. Every calculation footnote — 95 of them on MSFT #1 — carries a Python module path and a git hash; 47 source footnotes carry `tier T1_REGULATORY`.
items.rootCause: There is a human vocabulary and the document cannot reach it. `METRIC_WORDS` maps every metric to a reader's phrase (src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:626-713) and lives in `aer.web`, which `aer.render` must not import; so `CoverageNote.sentence` joins `Evaluation.metric` raw (src/aer/render/document.py:265-271, fed by :715-721) while, two lines away, failed *sections* are resolved to their titles. `_validation_row` puts `row.metric` and `str(row.value)` straight into the table (src/aer/sections/deterministic.py:272-301). The footnote types carry `tier`, `function_ref` and `code_version_prefix` as fields and the renderers print them (src/aer/render/document.py:290-313; src/aer/render/markdown.py:302-326). On the gate pages the key beside the title is deliberate — src/aer/web/templates/plans/review.html:60-61 prints both, because "the worker terminal speaks in keys".
evidence: Aggregate over docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/*/screens/*.json `raw_tokens`: 135 distinct identifiers; executive_summary, investment_thesis, key_risks, scenarios_sensitivities and segment_analysis on 16 screens each
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/mtb/report.md:14 — the coverage notice naming two metrics by code identifier; :479-505 — the validation table with `0E-8` and raw twelve-place decimals
Counted in the exported reports: msft1 47 `tier T…` footnotes and 95 `code version` footnotes; azn2 37 and 111; mtb 22 and 76
src/aer/render/document.py:265-271, :715-721; src/aer/sections/deterministic.py:272-301; src/aer/render/markdown.py:302-326
src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:615-717 — the words that exist and cannot be reached from the renderer
Audit §4.2 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:359) and F-25 (:905-922), where the same class of defect made the platform fail its own presentation check
items.recommendation: Move `METRIC_WORDS` (and the tier words) out of `aer.web.vocabulary` into a neutral module both the renderer and the interface import — `aer.core` or a small `aer.vocabulary` — and have the coverage notice and the validation table name a check the way they already name a section. Render scores through the existing house-style door rather than `str(Decimal)`. On the footnotes, keep the module path and code version but move them behind the same line the audit trail already uses, and translate the tier into words. On the gate pages the raw key is a decision rather than a defect: it belongs behind a disclosure or a developer toggle, not beside every title on the first page an operator ever sees. Extend the existing `presentation_integrity` scan to fail on a bare metric identifier and on an unformatted decimal in reader prose, so this cannot return.
items.tests: `tests/test_report_document.py::TheCoverageNoticeNamesAChecksWordsNotItsKey` — a run with `figure_plausibility` failing renders "Figures outside a sane range" and no underscore token, and `presentation_integrity` scores zero on its own output. `tests/test_plausibility.py` already holds the sister case for ADR names (F-25), so this is the same shape.
items.acceptance: Re-assemble the MTB document from its own record: the coverage notice and the validation appendix contain no snake_case identifier and no raw Decimal, and the presentation check still scores 0 failures.
items.challengeNote: 'lives in aer.web, which aer.render must not import' is an architectural argument, not an enforced rule: there is no import-linter contract in pyproject.toml, no ADR stating it, and src/aer/web/__init__.py has no eager imports, so `from aer.web.vocabulary import METRIC_WORDS` would mechanically work today. State it as the layering reason it is (aer.web already imports aer.render at web/figures.py:33 and pages.py:81-84, so the reverse inverts the layering) rather than as an impossibility — the neutral-module fix is still the right one. Effort: a session is tight for three renderers plus the deterministic section plus extending the presentation scan; call it one to two.

items.title: The exported document drops the verified excerpt, so the platform's one advantage does not leave the interface
items.problem: Judges reading the exported Markdown alone found the platform no easier to check than the console, and all three sceptic reads said why: a fact footnote gives the companyfacts JSON URL with no XBRL concept name, no period and no unit, so checking one figure means downloading a multi-megabyte JSON and hunting for a matching value. The platform holds, for every one of those citations, the verbatim excerpt its own verifier re-read to confirm it — and prints none of it. Every figure in every report was verified against bytes that the reader is never shown.
items.rootCause: `SourceFootnote` carries number, title, url, publisher, publication date, retrieved date and tier and nothing else (src/aer/render/document.py:306-313), and `_footnotes` builds it from the source document alone (:740-790) even though the `CitationRef` names an extraction. `Extraction.excerpt` is "the text at the locator, verbatim … what a reviewer is shown and what a verifier compares against" (src/aer/db/models/extraction.py:78) and `Extraction.locator` holds the character range, page and box. None of it reaches the footnote in any of the three renderers.
evidence: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/judges/reads.json — azn2 sceptic: "Three routes, none of which gets you to a line in a document … all cite one of two identical entries for … companyfacts … with no XBRL concept name, no context or period id and no unit"; msft1 reader: "the reader must open a very large JSON and locate e.g. the FY2026 Revenues entry themselves"
Audit §4.1 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:341-347): "The platform's verifiability advantage lives in the interface, not in the document it exports"; §4.3 use case 9 (:383)
src/aer/render/document.py:306-313, :740-790
src/aer/render/markdown.py:317-326; src/aer/render/html.py:305-385
src/aer/db/models/extraction.py:63-81 — locator and excerpt, both stored
items.recommendation: Carry the extraction onto the footnote and print the locator and a bounded excerpt: for an XBRL fact the concept, period and unit the extractor recorded; for a document the quoted sentence with its page. The data is already stored, already hashed and already what code re-read to verify the citation, so this adds no evidence and breaks no invariant — it stops discarding evidence at the last step. This is the single change most likely to move a blind comparison on verifiability, which is the one dimension where the platform was already level.
items.tests: `tests/test_report_document.py::ASourceFootnoteCarriesTheExcerptTheVerifierRead` — a citation whose extraction holds a concept/period locator renders them in the footnote, the excerpt is bounded and quoted, and the presentation check still passes. Fails today because `SourceFootnote` has no field for it.
items.acceptance: Re-assemble AZN #2's document and pick three figures at random: each footnote names the tag, the period and the unit, or quotes the sentence and its page. Hand the exported Markdown to a reader with no access to the interface and they can check a figure without opening a multi-megabyte JSON.
items.challengeNote: Restate the root cause as 'the citation reference is keyed on the source document, and the extraction id the fragment already carries is treated as unrenderable metadata (sections/render.py:75-87)'. Add src/aer/sections/render.py and src/aer/services/exhibits.py to filesTouched. Effort stays about a session only if the disambiguation rule is decided up front (which extraction backs a given document-level citation when several do); otherwise two.
items.invariantRisk: Not an invariant, but a licence risk the item does not mention: source_document.licence_note exists (db/models/source_document.py:153) and `aer purge-licensed` (cli.py:801-830) exists because a terminated subscription obliges deletion of every stored payload, with only hashes and provenance surviving. A verbatim excerpt copied into the immutable, exported report artefact is a payload copy that the purge cannot reach. The rule needs stating — excerpt printed only for tiers whose licence permits redistribution — and that is arguably an ADR beside ADR 0030 and ADR 0031.

items.title: Every report leads with "no view reached", because the only line in src/ that writes a rating sets it to None
items.problem: The header of every research note this platform has produced reads "**Non-binding view:** no view reached". All six judges gave that as a first reason for not acting on the document; five of six said no investment view is stated. On a refresh run the planner is told the prior view was "no view reached" too, so the second report is built on the first one's silence. The operator — whose personal, non-binding view this is and who has just spent forty minutes approving every input to it — is never once asked what they think.
items.rootCause: `report.rating = None` and `report.confidence = None`, unconditionally, at src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3765-3766. That is the only assignment to `Report.rating` in the whole of `src/`. The column exists and is nullable by design (src/aer/db/models/report.py:12-14, :73), the disclaimer already says "Any rating expressed is a non-binding personal view" (src/aer/render/document.py:76-80), the renderer already prints whatever is there (src/aer/render/markdown.py:160-162), the report page and the Obsidian export already read it, and `history.prior_digest_for` already carries it into the next run's planner (src/aer/services/history.py:470) — every consumer is built and the producer is a hard-coded None.
evidence: src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3765 — the sole writer
grep for `\.rating\s*=` over src/ returns exactly that one line
src/aer/db/models/report.py:73 and :12-14 — the column and the note that it is a non-binding personal view

Audit §4.1 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:318-334): "Is an investment view stated? no (5 of 6)"; "the platform's header says 'Non-binding view: no view reached', so there is no thesis to act on"
Audit §4.3 use case 1 (:372): "Good as an evidence base; not a decision document"
src/aer/services/history.py:465-476 — the prior digest reads "no view reached" on every refresh
docs/adr/0087 — the authored half of a verdict is already an accepted pattern for a frozen subject, which a draft at gate 2 is
items.recommendation: Add the operator's own view to the final gate: beside Approve and Reject, a short non-binding view and a confidence, optional, written by the person who is approving and stored on the report row that already has the fields. Not a model output and not a number the platform computes — the operator's sentence, framed exactly as the disclaimer already frames it. It is the cheapest thing in this whole diagnosis and it addresses the single most-cited reason six judges would not act. Whether the platform should *also* carry an authored interpretation of the draft under ADR 0087 is a separate, larger question and belongs to whoever owns the document's argument; this item is only about giving the operator somewhere to say what they concluded.
items.adrSubject: The rating on a report is the approving operator's own non-binding view, recorded at the final gate with the approval, and no model and no calculation may write it.
items.tests: `tests/test_report_document.py::TheApproversViewReachesTheHeader` — approving with a view stores it on the report, the header renders it rather than "no view reached", approving without one still renders "no view reached", and no non-operator code path can set the column. Fails today.
items.acceptance: A run approved with a stated view produces a document whose header carries it and whose disclaimer still stands; the next run on the same company shows the planner that prior view instead of "no view reached".
items.challengeNote: 'stored on the report row that already has the fields' is only half true. Report.rating is String(32) (db/models/report.py:73) and confidence is Float. Thirty-two characters holds a label ('Constructive', 'Cautious, undervalued') and not 'a short non-binding view' sentence. Either the recommendation means a short label — say so, since it is what the header renders — or the item needs a migration and is no longer purely additive. Decide which in the ADR.
items.invariantRisk: None, provided the ADR says plainly that no model and no calculation may write the column: CLAUDE.md invariant 7 already forbids a skill file setting a rating, and ADR 0087's authored half is a model output, so the ADR must distinguish the operator's own view from 0087's authored verdict rather than lean on it.

items.title: An unexpected error in the interface renders a JSON blob telling the operator to report it to nobody
items.problem: MSFT #1 stopped at the unmapped-concepts gate and the page that clears it answered 500. What the operator saw was seventeen words of JSON — `internal_error`, a request id, and "An unexpected error occurred. The failure has been logged; quote the request id when reporting it." There is no link back to the run, nothing about what to do, and no one to report it to: this is a single-operator local tool. The gate could not be cleared from the product at all; the audit's driver only got past it by calling the service directly.
items.rootCause: One set of exception handlers serves both the JSON API and the HTML interface with no content negotiation. `_handle_unexpected_error` returns `problem_response(...)`, which is always a `JSONResponse` (src/aer/api/errors.py:162-173 and :60-90), and it is registered for bare `Exception` on the whole app (:176-187). The web has a perfectly good refusal page (src/aer/web/templates/runs/problem.html) used only by handlers that call `_problem` deliberately. The underlying 500 was F-10, a Jinja precedence bug on a branch no fixture had ever rendered.
evidence: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft1/screens/financials.json — status 500, 17 words, raw_tokens ["internal_error", "request_id"]
Audit F-10 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:576-594): "An operator using the product as documented cannot clear the gate"
src/aer/api/errors.py:48-51 ("quote the request id when reporting it"), :60-90 (JSONResponse), :162-187
src/aer/web/templates/runs/problem.html — the HTML refusal page that exists and is not reached
src/aer/api/app.py:167 — one registration for the whole app
items.recommendation: Negotiate on Accept: an HTML request gets the problem page with the request id, a plain sentence, and a link back to the run it came from; an API request keeps the Problem Details document unchanged. Change the generic sentence to name where the detail actually is (the worker log and the run console) rather than an absent support desk. Separately, and this is what stops the next F-10: give every gate page a browser test driven from a filing-shaped fixture that actually reaches it — the gate pages are exercised today by fixtures that either map every tag (so the page 404s) or report each concept once (so the multi-period branch never renders).
items.tests: `tests/test_web_errors.py::an_html_request_gets_a_page_not_a_problem_document` — force a template error on a run page with Accept: text/html and assert an HTML response carrying the request id and a link back to the run; assert the same path with Accept: application/json is byte-identical to today. Plus one browser test per gate against a multi-period filing fixture.
items.acceptance: No surface in the interface can answer with raw JSON. Every gate page renders under a fixture with more than one period per concept.
items.challengeNote: One handler serves both surfaces: _handle_unexpected_error (src/aer/api/errors.py:162-173) returns problem_response, which always constructs a JSONResponse (:58-90), and it is registered for bare Exception across the whole app (errors.py:176-187, called from api/app.py:167). _GENERIC_DETAIL at errors.py:48-51 is the 'quote the request id when reporting it' sentence. src/aer/web/templates/runs/problem.html exists and is reached only by handlers that call _problem deliberately. The msft1 financials screen export records the 500.

items.title: Starting a run or approving a gate with the queue unreachable silently does nothing
items.problem: The operator presses Start, or presses Approve at one of six gates, and is redirected to a console that says "Queued. The worker picks this up within a second or two." If Redis is unreachable nothing was enqueued, nothing will ever run, and the console goes on saying the same thing indefinitely — because the line that would have said otherwise is itself unavailable when Redis is down. The audit's own history records this shape: a resealed run "sat queued for a night because no worker was running".
items.rootCause: `enqueue_run` swallows every exception and returns None (src/aer/queue.py:112-142), by a deliberate decision recorded in its docstring. All three callers ignore the return value: start (src/aer/web/pages.py:187), resume (:555) and the gate approval (:1838). The console's honest line comes from `_queued_words`, which returns None on RedisError (src/aer/web/pages.py:373-376), so the template falls through to the optimistic default (src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:379).
evidence: src/aer/queue.py:112-142 — returns None on any failure
src/aer/web/pages.py:187, :555, :1838 — three call sites, no return checked
src/aer/web/pages.py:365-381 — `_queued_words` returns None precisely when Redis is unreachable
src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:376-380 — the fallback sentence
docs/plan/ROADMAP.md §2.1 (line ~205): "The resealed run then sat queued for a night because no worker was running"
items.recommendation: Keep `enqueue_run` non-fatal — refusing an approval because a background queue is down would be worse — but stop discarding the answer. Carry the failure into the redirect and have the console say "recorded, but the queue could not be reached; start it and press Continue", with the Continue button already on the page. Make the console's queued line say "queued, and the worker's health record cannot be read" when Redis is unreachable, rather than falling through to the reassuring default. Three small edits.
items.tests: `tests/test_web_console.py::a_run_queued_into_an_unreachable_queue_says_so` — patch the pool constructor to raise, start a run, and assert the console names the failure and offers Continue; assert the same page with a healthy worker is unchanged. Fails today.
items.acceptance: With Redis stopped, starting a run and approving a gate both produce a page that says nothing was queued and offers the action that fixes it. No surface claims a run will begin within seconds when nothing was enqueued.
items.challengeNote: Rewrite the problem around the start-a-run case, which is the one that shows the reassuring sentence, and describe the approve case as its own symptom (it is really the decided-gate-still-says-waiting loop). The fix is four edits, not three: carry the failure into the redirect; make the queued line honest when Redis is unreachable; fix the fallback at pages.py:433; and give an AWAITING_APPROVAL job whose gate is decided a re-queue or Continue action, since resume_service.UNRESUMABLE_STATUSES does not block it but the console's can_resume does. Still small — an hour to half a session.

items.title: The sector gate can only be approved or refused, and a wrong classification needs neither
items.problem: Resolving the filer's industry code made the sector gate reachable and immediately showed it has two answers: Approve and continue, which grants the mandate deciding which valuation models may run, and Reject and stop this run. An operator looking at a classification they believe is wrong — Microsoft's SIC 7372 proposes the early-stage-technology profile — has nowhere to say so. Approving puts a wrong sector label on the front of the note; rejecting costs the run.
items.rootCause: The decision vocabulary at every gate is the shared two-button frame (src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:118-123), backed by `Decision` — which already carries a third member, AMENDED, in both the enum (src/aer/core/enums.py:164-169) and the native Postgres type since migration 0001 (migrations/versions/0001_core_schema.py:70), with a label already in the interface vocabulary (src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:398) and no writer anywhere in src/. The gate frame has no concept of a correction, so the classifier's proposal is the only thing a person can agree or refuse.
evidence: Audit F-26 (docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09.md:923-943) and §8 item 4 (:1141-1147)
Audit F-23 (:867-884): "the sector gate offers 'Approve and continue' or 'Reject and stop this run' and nothing else"
src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:118-123 — the two buttons, shared by all seven gates
src/aer/core/enums.py:164-169; migrations/versions/0001_core_schema.py:70; src/aer/web/vocabulary.py:398

items.recommendation: This is the operator's call, per audit §8 item 4, and it comes in two parts. The narrow one: a third answer at the sector gate that records the operator's own classification with a reason and continues on the mandate that classification implies — the enum member and the label already exist, so it is a route, a form and a rule. The wider one, which only they can settle: whether the four profiles that block no valuation model should stop a run at all. Note the shared frame means a third button on one gate is a change to the frame all seven use, so the rule must be per-gate or the other six inherit an answer they have no meaning for.
items.adrSubject: A classification proposed from a filer's industry code may be corrected by the operator at the gate; the correction is the decision, it is recorded with its reason, and it sets the mandate.
items.tests: `tests/test_sector_gate.py::a_wrong_classification_can_be_corrected_rather_than_refused` — the gate accepts a corrected sector, records it as AMENDED with the reason, the mandate follows the correction, and the other six gates still offer exactly two answers. Fails today.
items.acceptance: A run whose SIC proposes a profile the operator disagrees with continues on the operator's classification, with the correction on the record and named in the report's sector note.
items.challengeNote: Narrow the problem to what actually remains: a filer the classifier puts in one of the four *blocking* profiles (bank, insurer, REIT, pre-revenue biotechnology) that the operator believes is wrong. That is a rarer case than the item implies, and with F-23's fix the sector gate now fires only on banks and their kin, so impact is closer to small than moderate — reorder it behind the items that fire on every run. The wider question the item raises second (should non-blocking profiles stop a run) is already answered in code: they do not.
items.invariantRisk: ADR 0029 ('the sector block is a type not a check') governs how a sector profile grants or blocks a mandate; a third answer that lets an operator set the classification directly must record the correction as the input to mandate resolution rather than as a bypass of the type, and the new ADR should name 0029 as the record it extends.

items.title: `revise` is serial and costs 10–11 minutes of every run
items.problem: After the adversary reports, the run spends 10.1 minutes (azn2), 11.3 (msft2) and 10.1 (mtb) redrafting at most four sections one after another, with nothing shown to the operator. It is the single largest step in the run — larger than `draft`, which does four and a half times as much work — and it is 28–34% of the total machine time.
items.rootCause: `revise_challenged_sections` walks its targets in a plain `for target in targets:` loop on the caller's session (src/aer/services/revision.py:190), bounded by `MAX_REVISED_SECTIONS = 4` (src/aer/services/revision.py:80). The identical work in `draft` already fans out four-wide over a session factory with a drain-never-abandon gather (`_drafted_apart`, src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3281-3317); `revise` never got the same treatment. Serialisation is provable from the record, not inferred: the step's duration equals the sum of its own model-call latencies — 606.6s of calls against a 607.6s step (azn2), 675.9 against 677.1 (msft2), 602.2 against 603.5 (mtb).
evidence: docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/azn2/steps.json — revise 607.6s; run-export.json model_calls for step `revise`: 5 calls summing 606.6s
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/msft2/steps.json — revise 677.1s; 6 calls summing 675.9s
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/mtb/steps.json — revise 603.5s; 6 calls summing 602.2s
src/aer/services/revision.py:190 (`for target in targets:`), :80 (`MAX_REVISED_SECTIONS = 4`)
src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3281-3317 (`_drafted_apart`, the pattern to copy)
ADR 0091 bounds the count ("at most four sections revise, most severe first") and says nothing about scheduling
items.recommendation: Fan revise out at the same bound draft already uses, by the same mechanism. List-scheduling the recorded per-call latencies at four-wide gives 208.6s (azn2), 211.8s (msft2), 167.9s (mtb); inflating by the 8–26% overhead the same model under-predicts `draft` by, expect roughly 200–255s — a saving of 5.6–7.1 minutes, or 18–20% of the whole run. No ADR is needed: ADR 0091 fixes the bound, not the order of execution, and the sections are as independent of each other in revise as they are in draft. Two implementation constraints, both visible in the existing code: the `delete(RevisionNote ...)` that opens the function (src/aer/services/revision.py:166-172) must run and commit on the coordinator session before any worker starts, and `fill_deterministic_sections` must stay on the coordinator after the wave drains, because it describes the record the wave just changed. Land it with or after audit §8 item 6 (F-21, sibling calls cannot see each other's spend) rather than before it.

options.cost: A session. Adds no new kind of budget exposure — four concurrent writer calls is exactly what `draft` already runs.
options.risk: Widens the cap-overshoot window for this step to 4 × one call's projection, the same window draft already accepts (src/aer/agents/base.py:481-511 checks committed spend before each call).

options.name: Two-wide
options.change: Same change, semaphore at 2.
options.cost: A session. Saves ~4.4 min instead of ~6.5.
options.risk: Halves the overshoot-window increase. The conservative choice if F-21 is still open.

options.name: Leave it serial
options.change: Nothing.
options.risk: Keeps a third of the run in the one place the operator sees nothing.

items.tests: A test with a fake provider whose section calls sleep a known interval: four targets must complete in materially less than the serial sum, and the stored `revisions` list must come back in severity order regardless of completion order — the same reassembly guarantee `_draft` already states ("Reassembled in declared order — the sections' own, never completion order", src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:3378-3380). A second test asserts the RevisionNote delete happens exactly once and before any worker writes.
items.acceptance: On the next live run of the same subject, the `revise` row in `steps.json` is under 300s where the audit recorded 600s+, the gate-2 payload's `revisions` block contains the same section keys and dispositions as before, and the payload hash is still sealed by `revise`.
items.challengeNote: Expect roughly 210–280s for a 4-wide revise, not 168–212s — a saving of about 5.5–6.5 minutes (17–19% of merged machine time), not 5.6–7.1. Drop the 'largest step in the run' claim: revise exceeds draft on two of five audited runs. Add the counter/over-bound ordering and per-worker spend accumulation to the implementation constraints, and read tests/test_revision_loop.py (731 lines, including `test_the_bound_holds_and_the_overflow_is_named`) before confirming 'a session'.

items.title: The one-page summary and the live preview already exist and are linked from nowhere a running run can reach
items.problem: The complaint is "nothing useful exists at ten minutes". Two routes that would answer it are already built and shipped: `/runs/{job_id}/preview` renders the document as it stands from live rows, and `/runs/{job_id}/summary` renders the at-a-glance block plus the executive summary and key risks. Neither is reachable while a run is running. `/preview` is linked only from the gate-2 review page and the footnote drill-down; `/summary` is linked from no template at all — it is registered as a known page and orphaned.
items.rootCause: The console's whole decision block, including the only link to `/runs/{id}/review`, sits inside `{% if awaiting %}` (src/aer/web/templates/runs/console.html:64, link at :104-105), so a RUNNING run shows evidence counts and step keys and nothing readable. `/runs/{job_id}/summary` (src/aer/web/pages.py:1377-1413) appears in the shell's known-pages registry (src/aer/web/shell/registry.py:192) under the comment "reached from the run itself", but `grep` over src/aer/web/templates finds no `href` to it anywhere. Both routes already tolerate a half-written run: they require only that `report_sections` rows exist, which they do from the end of the `plan` step (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:767), and `assemble_document` renders a PENDING section with a status note rather than failing (src/aer/render/document.py:108-112, :504-524).
evidence: src/aer/web/pages.py:1337 (`/runs/{job_id}/preview`), :1378 (`/runs/{job_id}/summary`)

(src/aer/render/document.py:109) — true of a finished report, misleading on a run still writing. This is the cheapest single move in this area: it converts an existing, tested renderer into the answer to use case 7 for zero model spend. The one thing it must not do is offer a decision: the gate-2 form renders on `{% if not decided %}` (src/aer/web/templates/runs/_gate.html:57), so link the read-only preview and summary, never `/runs/{id}/review`.

items.adrSubject: A read-only view of a run in progress is not "seeing the draft" in ADR 0091's sense, and carries no approval control
items.tests: A route test that the console rendered for a RUNNING job contains hrefs to `/runs/{id}/summary` and `/runs/{id}/preview`, and does not contain one to `/runs/{id}/review`. A second that `/runs/{id}/summary` answers 200 for a job whose sections are all PENDING, showing the at-a-glance block and a "still being written" line per section. A third that neither page renders an approve control at any job status.

items.challengeNote: Two framing errors. `whichIssue: 'both'` is not supported — no judge finding I can locate cites latency; the console won on content (no view, focus questions unanswered, figures withheld), so this is a user-ready item. And the item sets `adrNeeded: true` while its options table punts the ADR question to the next item; decide one way. Also note the PENDING string at document.py:109 is shared with the rendered report and the PDF, so changing it changes finished documents too — the tests listed do not cover that.
items.invariantRisk: ADR 0091 states the revision happens 'before a person ever sees the draft'. Linking either surface while a run is RUNNING lets a person see the draft before `revise`, so the ADR the item flags is genuinely required for both options, not only for the preview.

items.title: The document is complete at 17–23 minutes and the operator may not see it until 30–37
items.problem: With the operator's waits collapsed out, the eighteen-section draft finishes at 16.80 minutes (azn2), 16.57 (msft2) and 22.69 (mtb). Gate 2 — the first moment anything readable is offered — arrives at 30.03, 30.87 and 36.78. The 13.2–14.3 minutes in between are `validate`, `red_team`, `revise`, `verdict` and `brief_challenges`, during which the console shows a step key and a spend figure. That window alone is longer than the console baseline's entire time to answer on M&T (14.1 minutes).
items.rootCause: ADR 0091 is explicit that the sections material challenges attack are redrafted "before a person ever sees the draft", and the gate-2 hash is sealed by `revise` (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:1808-1861). That is a deliberate quality decision, and it has the side effect that a finished, validated, cited draft is withheld for a quarter of an hour with no interim surface. Nothing in the code publishes the pre-adversary draft; nothing shows the adversary's progress either.
evidence: Collapsed-clock schedules recomputed from docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/{azn2,msft2,mtb}/steps.json: draft ends 1007.9s / 993.9s / 1361.3s; gate_final opens 1799.1s / 1850.0s / 2203.4s

items.recommendation: Shrink the window with the free fixes first — concurrent revise takes it from 13.2–14.3 minutes to roughly 7–8 — and then publish into what is left rather than lengthening the spine. Publishing the unreviewed draft is the only route to a genuinely useful ten-minute artefact, and it is the one option in this area that trades something real: the platform's claim is that a person never meets a draft the adversary has not attacked. If it is taken, take it as a type, the way ADR 0034 handles a withheld figure — a first-read view that carries no approval control, no PDF path, no export, and a standing banner naming what has not run yet. Do not shorten the spine by dropping the adversary: `red_team` is 2.3–3.2 minutes and £0.28–0.39, it is the step that caught a section contradicting its own citation, and removing it would trade the platform's only clear win over the console for three minutes.

options.name: Shrink only
options.change: Concurrent revise (and a wider draft fan-out); publish nothing early.
options.risk: Gate 2 lands at ~22–25 min instead of 30–37. Still nothing at ten minutes.

options.name: Publish the unreviewed draft as a typed first read
options.change: A read-only view, no approve control, banner naming that the adversary and the revision have not run.
options.cost: A session on top of the previous item, plus an ADR.
options.risk: An operator could act on a draft the red team would have changed. On the audit's runs, revise touched at most four of eighteen sections, so most of what they would read is what they would have got — but the sections it touched were executive_summary and investment_thesis on four of five runs, which are exactly the ones a reader reads first.

options.name: Run the adversary per wave
options.change: Attack sections as they land rather than once over the whole draft.
options.cost: A few sessions; changes what the adversary sees.
options.risk: Refused on the merits: ADR 0039's adversary sees the whole claim set and the evidence index, which is how it finds cross-section contradictions. Splitting it multiplies calls and narrows its view.

items.adrSubject: A first read is a type with no approval, no export and no PDF, and its banner names every step that has not run
items.tests: A test that the first-read view renders for a job whose `red_team` step has not started, carries the banner, and exposes no form that posts to any gate route. A test that `record_decision` still refuses a FINAL decision whose payload hash predates `revise`'s seal (this must remain true and is the guard the whole option rests on).
items.acceptance: On a live run, a readable document exists on screen at the moment `draft` finishes — 16–23 minutes today, 12–17 after the concurrency fixes — and the only way to approve anything is still gate 2 on the sealed payload.
items.challengeNote: Reclassify from 'both' to user-ready. State plainly that the typed first read has no verdict and no revision, i.e. it is strictly less of a decision document than the one six judges already refused; its value is that the operator can stop waiting, not that it competes with the console. The acceptance criterion ('a readable document exists on screen at the moment draft finishes') is measurable and fine.
items.invariantRisk: ADR 0091's 'before a person ever sees the draft' and ADR 0087's verdict placement both bear on this; the item flags one ADR, and the new one must name both. The suggested guard — record_decision still refusing a FINAL decision on a payload hash predating revise's seal — is real and already enforced (src/aer/services/approvals.py:96-133 requires the hash of what was shown).

items.title: A complete, deterministic front page is computable at 6–11 minutes and is never rendered until the run ends
items.problem: Every figure a research note is read for on its first page — the latest period's revenue, net income and EPS, the annual series, the headline ratios — is derived by deterministic code from hashed facts and exists long before any prose. On the collapsed clock the facts land at 5.86/7.79/9.60 minutes and the valuation is struck at 7.72/9.93/11.33. None of it reaches a document-shaped surface until `render`, which runs after gate 2 at 30–37 minutes. The console offers three evidence links instead — Sources, Claims, Valuation — which are tables of machinery, not an answer.
items.rootCause: `glance_content` (src/aer/render/glance.py:202-238) reads only `financial_facts` scoped to the subject and the run's headline ratio rows — the outputs of `extract` and `calculate` — and makes no model call. It is invoked only from `assemble_document` (src/aer/render/document.py:482-494), which is invoked from `_run_document` on the preview, summary and footnote pages and from `render`. Since none of those preview pages is reachable during a run (previous item), the block never renders early. Nothing else is wrong with it: it already withholds itself with a stated reason when the figures are not all the subject's or the relations among them are impossible, which is what refused M&T's front page.

items.recommendation: Render the at-a-glance block, the valuation summary and the comps note as soon as `calculate` and `value` have run, on the same page as the first-read surface. This is the one option here that is unambiguously free of any ADR question: these are deterministic figures the report would show anyway, computed by code, withheld by the same plausibility guard, and seeing them early pre-empts no approval — gate 2 approves the drafted document, and no figure on the front page changes between minute eight and minute thirty. It is also the honest answer to "a first read in ten minutes": numbers at eight minutes on every subject measured, prose a few minutes later.

options.cost: An hour on top of linking the page.
options.risk: None to any invariant. The block already refuses itself when the figures do not hold together.

options.change: Hold the page until executive_summary, investment_thesis and key_risks have landed.
options.cost: A session, plus a drafting-order change.
options.risk: Pushes the first read to 10.5–15 min and inherits the previous item's ADR question.

options.name: Leave it until render
options.change: Nothing.
options.risk: Keeps the platform's strongest, cheapest, most defensible output invisible for twenty-two minutes.

items.tests: A test that `glance_content` returns content for a job that has run only `acquire`, `extract` and `calculate`, and that the summary page renders it with every section marked unwritten. A test that a job whose facts fail the relation check still renders the withheld notice rather than a partial block (the M&T case).
items.acceptance: On a live run of any of the three audited subjects, the run console at ten minutes shows the latest reported period's revenue, net income and EPS with footnote markers that resolve, and — where a subscription exists — the market capitalisation and the struck valuation.
items.challengeNote: Rewrite the acceptance to what glance can actually produce at eight minutes: latest-period revenue, net income and EPS with resolving footnote markers, the five-year revenue strip, the margin/FCF/net-debt ratios, and — once `value` has run — WACC and value per share (base case). Drop market capitalisation, or make adding it to the headline set an explicit sub-item. Note also that the summary page keeps only `one_pager` sections (migration 0040: executive summary and key risks), so at eight minutes it shows the glance plus two 'still being written' lines and nothing else.

items.title: Five minutes of planning block acquisition and extraction that depend on nothing the planner produces
items.problem: The first thing that happens on every run is 5.1–5.6 minutes of `plan` and `critique_plan`, during which nothing is fetched and nothing is extracted. On the bank, `extract` alone then takes a further 3.6 minutes before the first figure exists. The operator's first decision arrives at 5.11/5.31/5.58 minutes with nothing behind it but a model's proposal, and the four decisions that follow are strung out behind a chain that could largely have run in parallel with it.
items.rootCause: `build_steps` declares `acquire`, `classify` and `extract` with no `needs`, so the engine's chain default places each after the previously declared step (src/aer/workflow/engine.py:447-450) — which puts them behind `gate_plan`. Nothing in them reads the plan: `_acquire` resolves the entity from `request.ticker` and `request.exchange` and fetches from EDGAR (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2211-2297); `_classify` reads only `acquire`'s output; `_extract` reads the archived aggregate by hash and filters on `request.work_order.as_of_date` (:2782-2830). The section list is resolved from the request before the planner is asked, and the docstring says so outright — "the planner proposes focus, never the section list" (:687-690). All three cost nothing: every `acquire`, `classify` and `extract` row in every run's steps.json carries `cost_gbp: 0`, and F-06 confirms no acquisition in the pass spent money.
evidence: src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:398-460 (declaration order), :2211-2297 (`_acquire`), :2782-2830 (`_extract`), :687-690
src/aer/workflow/engine.py:447-450 (the chain default)
docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/{azn2,msft2,mtb}/steps.json — acquire+classify+extract = 29.1s / 135.2s / 226.7s; plan+critique_plan = 306.5s / 318.6s / 334.8s
audit F-06: "every acquisition in this pass was free"
src/aer/web/gates.py:70-73 — gate 1's stated consequence: "Everything expensive in the run is downstream of this page"
items.recommendation: Give `acquire`, `classify` and `extract` an explicit `needs` that does not include `gate_plan`, so they run in the same wave as `plan` and `critique_plan`. On the bank this removes 3.8 minutes from the critical path outright; on MSFT 2.3; on AZN 0.5. It also makes the unmapped-concepts payload exist by the time gate 1 is offered, which is the precondition for batching the decisions. Keep `propose_peers` and `propose_themes` behind gate 1: they cost £0.013 and £0.012 of model spend, and moving them would make gates.py:70-73's sentence false. That is the exact line to hold — move what is free, leave what is paid. The change still needs an ADR, because a rejected plan would leave the platform having fetched from EDGAR; the honest answer is that the documents are hashed, stored and reusable by the next run on the same filer, and that the request itself is the operator's authorisation to look the company up.

options.name: Move the three free steps into the planning wave
options.change: Explicit `needs` on acquire/classify/extract; gate_plan keeps every paid step behind it.
options.cost: A few sessions with the ADR and the graph tests.
options.risk: Fetches before approval. No model spend, no cap exposure, and the artefacts survive a rejection.

options.name: Move extract only
options.change: Leave acquire behind the gate, which makes the move worthless — extract needs the artefact.
options.risk: Refused on inspection: there is nothing to extract before acquisition.

options.name: Shorten the spine by cutting the plan critic
options.change: Drop `critique_plan`, saving 2.5–3.5 min and £0.29–0.39.
options.cost: An ADR superseding half of ADR 0091.
options.risk: Refused on the merits. The critic returned six challenges and provoked a planner revision on all six audited runs, and its output sits inside the gate-1 hash — approving a plan means approving it with the critique in view. Cutting it buys three minutes and removes the reason gate 1 is worth stopping for.

items.adrSubject: Acquisition and extraction are free and request-driven, so they run beside the plan; gate 1 still holds back everything that spends
items.tests: A graph test that the engine's first wave contains `plan`, `acquire`, `classify` and `extract` and that no step with a non-zero `estimated_cost_gbp` is schedulable before `gate_plan` succeeds. A test that a run rejected at gate 1 has recorded source documents and facts and spent £0 on models.
items.acceptance: On a live M&T run, gate 1 and the unmapped-concepts gate are both offered inside six minutes, against 5.6 and 9.6 today, and the plan gate's own step timings are unchanged.
items.challengeNote: Before costing this, establish what the engine does when two gate nodes can pause in the same wave, and whether a job can hold two AWAITING_APPROVAL gates. If it cannot, extract must stay behind gate_plan and the item collapses to moving acquire+classify, worth about 10 seconds — i.e. not worth an ADR. Restate the benefit as 'up to 3.8 minutes on a large filer, 0.5 on a small one'.
items.invariantRisk: No CLAUDE.md invariant is broken — point-in-time is still enforced at acquisition and no model spends. But src/aer/web/gates.py:70-73 states 'Everything expensive in the run is downstream of this page' as the PLAN gate's recorded consequence, and fetching from EDGAR before approval makes that sentence partly false even at zero cost; ADR 0009 (egress is deterministic and guarded) and ADR 0022 (the FCA NSM is not fetched automatically) are the house precedents the new ADR has to argue against.

items.title: `extract` scales linearly with the fact count at ~9 ms each, because it scans the whole document once per fact
items.problem: On the two large filers `extract` takes 2.6 minutes (MSFT, 18,610 facts) and 3.6 minutes (M&T, 23,174 facts) of pure deterministic Python on the critical path, before any figure exists and before the unmapped-concepts gate can be offered. It is the third-largest non-model step in the run and it is entirely under the platform's control.
items.rootCause: After persisting the facts, `_extract` loops over every chosen fact and calls `extracted.locate(...)` twice in the miss case (src/aer/workflow/workflows/vertical_slice_v1.py:2818-2821). `ExtractedText.locate` is `self.text.find(needle, start)` with `start` defaulting to 0 (src/aer/core/schemas/extraction.py:385-392), so each fact re-scans the whole extracted companyfacts text from the beginning. Cost per chosen fact is flat across three different filers and two different fact counts: 37.3s/4,181 = 8.9 ms (AZN), 156.8s/18,610 = 8.4 ms (MSFT #1), 216.0s/23,174 = 9.3 ms (M&T). That the cost tracks *chosen* facts rather than *written* ones is the confirming detail — msft2 and mtb wrote zero facts (the rows already existed) and still took 128.7s and 216.7s.
