items.recommendation: Both, and replay first. This is the cheapest defence of the platform's strongest claim, and §4.14's history is the argument: `cited_figure_agreement` exists because the red team caught a contradicted figure twice in two live runs, and it was built at threshold zero rather than as a tolerance. The same reasoning applies to the fact side. An ADR is needed only if the figure-reading rule itself changes — ADR 0060 governs what counts as a figure, and adding the scale word to the comparison is within it; extending the agreement check to facts is a new rule and should be recorded.
items.adrSubject: A numeric claim naming a fact must state that fact's figure, and a figure's scale word is part of the figure.
items.tests: A test that "$331.8 million" against a stored 331,839,000,000 is refused; a test that a claim citing a fact and misstating its value is refused while one citing a fact without printing it passes; replay of the five archived runs recording how many claims each rule would have cost.
items.acceptance: `aer replay-draft` over the audit's five archived runs reports the refusal count each new rule would cause, and it is small enough to accept; a synthetic wrong-scale claim is refused.
items.challengeNote: The ADR framing is wrong in a way that matters. ADR 0109 — `docs/adr/0109-a-numeric-claim-stands-on-the-figure-it-names.md`, Accepted 2026-09-05 — already decided that naming a fact or calculation by id *is* a numeric claim's evidence and removed the requirement to carry a citation at all. That makes the missing value check strictly more load-bearing than before (a fact-backed numeric claim now stands on an id whose value nothing compares to the prose), and it means the record to write is an amendment to ADR 0109, whose title is almost the proposed adrSubject verbatim — not a new ADR. The item cites ADR 0060 and never mentions 0109. Also correct the location: the fact-side gap is in `src/aer/services/evaluations.py:569-588`, not `core/figures.py` (the audit's own imprecision, inherited here); only the scale-word half is in figures.py. Replace the non-existent `src/aer/services/claims` and `src/aer/services/evaluation` in filesTouched.
items.invariantRisk: None — both changes tighten invariant 3's enforcement. The record is an amendment to ADR 0109 (and, for the scale word, within ADR 0060), not a new decision.

items.title: Add §8.6 to §2 — the per-run cap can be jointly overshot, which is invariant 6's own failure mode
items.problem: Inside the research wave and the draft fan-out, five and four concurrent sessions each see only committed cost rows, so none can see its siblings' spend and the per-run cap can be jointly overshot by up to (N-1) times one call's worst case. Separately, cost rows flushed by a step that dies mid-flight are lost — consistent with AZN's `revise` attempt 0, a minute of calls and no rows. CLAUDE.md's invariant 6 says "Caps that only warn are caps that do not work"; a cap that N siblings can each pass individually is the same shape of thing.
items.rootCause: Cost is published when the step commits, per ADR 0016's rule that a run publishes itself step by step. Both fixes require committing cost rows inside a step, which amends that rule.
evidence: Readiness audit F-21, first bullet — the (N-1) bound and the lost rows, with AZN's revise attempt 0 named
Readiness audit §8 item 6 — "Both fixes publish cost before the step commits, which amends ADR 0016's publication rule"
CLAUDE.md invariant 6
docs/adr/0016-a-run-publishes-itself-step-by-step.md
Readiness audit §3.3 — no run breached its cap in this pass, so the exposure is latent rather than observed

options.name: Publish cost inside the step

options.risk: It puts a second write path into a step's transaction boundary; the ADR must say what a cost row's visibility means for a step that then fails.

options.name: Reserve the worst case up front
options.change: Each sibling reserves its per-call ceiling before it runs and releases the difference, so the cap holds without changing publication.
options.risk: Over-reserves and can refuse work the budget could have afforded; ADR 0052 and 0053 already say a step with no estimate is a step with no cap, so the estimates exist.

items.recommendation: The operator's, because it amends a recorded decision — but I would take it, and early, because it is the only item in this whole map that touches an invariant's enforcement rather than the product's usefulness. Note that it is genuinely small work behind a genuinely real ADR, so the ADR is the schedule.
items.adrSubject: A cost row is published when the call returns, not when the step commits — what that means for a step that then fails, and for the gate hash that quotes the spend.
items.tests: A test that N concurrent siblings under a cap that N-1 of them would exhaust are refused at the right one; a test that a step killed mid-flight leaves its cost rows behind.
items.acceptance: A fake-provider run with a deliberately tight cap and a fanned-out step stops at the cap rather than past it, and a killed step's spend appears in the run's ledger.
items.challengeNote: F-21's first bullet (readiness-audit-2026-09.md:761-770) states the (N−1) bound, the five-and-four sibling counts and AZN's `revise` attempt 0 exactly as reproduced, and §8 item 6 says "Both fixes publish cost before the step commits, which amends ADR 0016's publication rule". `docs/adr/0016-a-run-publishes-itself-step-by-step.md` exists. CLAUDE.md invariant 6 says "Caps that only warn are caps that do not work", and the argument that a cap N siblings can each pass individually is the same shape of failure is sound. §3.3 confirms no run breached, so the exposure is latent — which is the correct reason to file it rather than to treat it as a bug. The acceptance test (a fake-provider run under a tight cap with a fanned-out step) is measurable in the suite with no spend, honouring the no-network/no-model-spend test rule.
items.invariantRisk: Amends ADR 0016, correctly flagged and correctly made the operator's call. The second option (reserve the worst case up front) would not amend 0016 and is the cheaper path to invariant 6 — the item is right that ADRs 0052/0053 already require per-step estimates, so reservation has the inputs it needs. Worth putting that asymmetry to the operator: one option needs an ADR and one does not.

items.title: Leave alone: Phase 6 (A5, A7, A8), the whole Decided-against list, and the closed judgement layer
items.problem: The risk in a plan this size is that it reaches for items that look adjacent and are not. Three groups should not move. The Phase-6 gate — no authentication (`get_current_user` returns the first row of `users`), no inbound rate limiting, no production deployment story — is gated on intent to leave one machine, and neither issue creates that intent: the product is one operator, one laptop, one report at a time. The Decided-against list (trade execution, a portfolio optimiser, multi-user, investment advice, a positions table, a currency-exchange kind, a Bank of England adapter, FCA NSM fetching, an external tracing vendor) must stay decided; in particular a stated view must not become investment advice, which is the failure mode closest to the item this plan most wants. And §3.5-§3.11's judgement layer is closed in its forced dependency order — nothing here should reopen it.
items.rootCause: Not a defect. The risk is planning drift: 'user ready' sounds like it implies authentication and deployment, and 'better than the console' sounds like it implies a recommendation.

items.title: The cheapest credible re-measurement of ISSUE 2: two subjects, three runs, no new baselines, £31.50
items.problem: The audit's practical verdict cost six live runs and three console baselines to set up (£63.32 of the £100 ceiling, §7). Nobody has written down what a repeat costs or contains, so the instinct after the fixes land will be either to re-run everything at ~£60 or to re-run nothing and declare victory from a mechanical scorer — which is exactly the trap §4.1 sprang, where every mechanical check passed the report the judges refused to act on.
items.rootCause: Not a code fault. There is no re-measurement protocol anywhere in the repository: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/audit/ holds driver/, scoring/, baseline/ and report/, and no plan document and no judging module. The subjects, the policy and the brief are all pinned in code (audit/subjects.py, audit/driver/policy.py, audit/baseline/brief.py), so the expensive half is already reproducible and only the design is missing.

Audit §7: baselines £7.63 (MSFT), £11.03 (AZN), £6.71 (MTB)

Audit §4.3 use case 2: MSFT's second run is the refresh case, so a second run on one subject is not a duplicate
items.recommendation: Recommended design, £31.50: three platform runs (MSFT ×2 — the second doubles as the refresh use case and gives the run-to-run variance check free — plus AZN ×1) at a budgeted £8 each = £24; zero new baselines, reusing the three September notes; 18 judged reads and 9 blind comparisons at roughly £2.50 per subject-pair = £7.50. That fits inside the £36.68 the audit left unspent. The floor, if money is tight, is £21: MSFT ×1 and AZN ×1, twelve reads and six comparisons. Add MTB (+£8 run, +£2.50 judging) only if the operator has taken §8's decision 2 on a bank's revenue, because until then no bank produces an approvable report to judge. Judge cost is my arithmetic from the platform's own price table (claude-opus-5 at $5.00/$25.00 per million, src/aer/providers/costs.py:84, usd_to_gbp 0.79 at src/aer/config.py:369) over ~100KB documents; the September round was paid in session tokens and never priced, so treat it as an estimate. The spend is the operator's call, which is why both designs are given. Anti-gaming clause, pre-registered: every run commissioned inside the measurement window is judged, and none is discarded for reading badly.

So a platform run re-measured in, say, December reads whatever has been filed since, while the September notes are three months stale on news and prices — and "better on recent developments" is one of the six comparison dimensions the platform lost 9 of 9 times.

The September baselines are dated 2026-09-11 (MSFT, AZN) and 2026-09-12 (MTB) in docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/baseline/*/summary.json; the platform runs were stamped 2026-09-12.

items.recommendation: Reuse all three notes and state the asymmetry in the protocol rather than pretending it away, then spend on a freshness control only when it could change the verdict. The asymmetry is not symmetric in effect: a stale console note is a *lower bound* on the console, so if the platform still loses against it the result is conclusive and no control is needed. Buy one fresh MSFT baseline (£7.63, the cheapest of the three) only if the platform wins, and only to check the win survives a same-week comparator. Re-measure soon after the fixes land, so the filing set has not moved: MSFT's FY2026 10-K of 29 July 2026 and AZN's FY2025 20-F are what both sides read. Do not restore an operator-typed as-of date to make the audit cheaper — ADR 0110 refused that field because a wrong date fails silently, and reversing a recorded decision for the convenience of measuring it is the worst reason available.

items.title: The instrument that produced the practical verdict exists only as its output
items.problem: The audit's headline finding — six of six blind comparisons chose the console — came from eighteen agent reads and nine comparisons under a fixed rubric. None of that is code. A repeat would rebuild the rubric from a 497KB JSON file by hand, and any drift in the wording of a rubric key silently changes what the new round is measuring, which makes the two rounds incomparable at exactly the moment the operator needs them compared.
items.rootCause: audit/ contains driver/, scoring/, baseline/, report/, ledger.py, subjects.py and smoke.py — and no judging module. The rubric survives only as the key set of docs/plan/readiness-audit-2026-09/judges/reads.json: fourteen keys per read (focus_questions, checklist, view_stated, view_argued_not_recited, bear_case_in_the_body, numbers_explained, verifiability, still_to_look_up, would_act_on_it, first_thing_to_check, reading_minutes, strongest_paragraph, weakest_paragraph, overall) and nine per comparison, with a ten-item checklist and three lenses.
evidence: /home/user/AgeanticInvestmentPlatform/audit/ — no judging package (ls of the audit tree)

Audit §2: "The practitioner reads did complete, on the second attempt: three judges for each of four documents and three blind pairwise comparisons per subject, all eighteen agents"
Audit §6: "The judges found what no scorer could" — F-27 and F-28 were found by a model reading the document as a document, and every mechanical check passed that report

Write the unblinding key to the harness's own file, never into the judge's prompt. Emit exactly the September shape so the two rounds compare row by row and the 54 dimension votes can be tallied the same way.

items.title: The comparison is blind to labels and not to format, and nothing measured whether the blind held
items.problem: A judge told "document A and document B" can tell in one line which machine wrote which. The platform report opens with a metadata block ending "**Non-binding view:** no view reached" and carries 95 footnotes of the form "Calculated: `gross margin = gross profit / revenue` = 0.6794 … code version `f17f7158e569`"; the console note opens with the model's own chat filler, "I'll research this thoroughly before writing. Let me begin with the primary sources." So "all six comparisons chose the console" may be partly "preferred the shape they expect a research note to have" — and nothing in the record distinguishes the two.
items.rootCause: The rubric has no key asking the judge to identify the documents. reads.json's `identity` is the harness's own unblinding key, not a judge's guess, so blinding integrity was assumed rather than measured.

items.title: ISSUE 1 needs a journey harness: it is a count, not an opinion, and nothing counts it today
items.problem: "A competent private investor can commission, steer, finish, recover and share research without a terminal, without dead ends, and without meeting a defect" is an adjective until somebody counts. The audit counted by hand from driver.jsonl and screenshots; the browser suite has a journey test that proves the surfaces join up but clears the conditional gates from inside the test process, so it never counts a gate an operator meets.
items.rootCause: tests/e2e/test_research_journey.py:133 advances past every conditional gate with `worker.advance_to_the_final_gate(job_id)` — deliberately, because the surfaces have their own tests — so the journey is proved to exist and never measured. tests/e2e/sweep.py is the hardening instrument (reflow, keyboard, colour scheme, scripting off) over STATIC_SURFACES and has the browser plumbing but none of the journey's assertions. The audit's own page scanner, audit/driver/screenshots.py:35-38 and :60-77, already extracts the four things a journey harness wants from a page — the payload hash, the approve control, raw snake_case tokens and a UUID count — and is invoked only for evidence capture, never as an assertion.

It drives the fake scene (StubSecClient plus the fake provider, so £0 and no network), clicks every gate including the conditional ones, and writes var/journey.json holding six numbers with stated bounds: gate stops met (expect 6 ordinary, 7 bank), values the operator had to supply or amend at the assumptions gate, forward controls present on every stopped state, pages whose visible text tells the reader to run a command, UUIDs and unledgered snake_case tokens in visible text, and operator actions from front page to rendered report. Reuse tests/e2e/worker.py for everything a worker would do and audit/driver/screenshots.py's two regexes for the vocabulary scan, so the harness and the audit measure the same thing the same way. It runs in its own pytest process, per the repository's two-process rule.
items.tests: The harness is the test. It must fail before the fixes: on today's tree it should report three states with no forward control (see the dead-end inventory) and at least one page requiring the terminal, and those rows go green only when the fixes land. A harness that is green on the first run is measuring nothing.

items.title: "No dead ends" needs a list of the dead ends, and three are already known and open
items.problem: ISSUE 1's central claim is that an operator never meets a state with no way forward. Three such states are documented and unfixed, and there is no list, so nothing asserts that any of them acquired an exit. Two of them cost a live run each in the audit: a £6.80 MSFT run that can neither be approved nor re-measured, and a bank that cannot be researched at all.
items.rootCause: F-16: the gate refuses a decision on a payload that has moved and refuses a second decision on the same gate, so the run has no exit. F-22: metrics are written at `validate` and nothing re-evaluates a finished job — src/aer/cli.py has acceptance, replay-run, resume, reseal and step commands and no re-evaluate. F-26: the sector gate offers "approve" and "reject" and no "not this sector". F-08 (stranded run) is fixed and proved three times, which is the shape the others should take.

items.title: "Minutes to a readable result" has no instrument: the audit's gate waits are the driver's polling intervals
items.problem: One of the five things ISSUE 1's harness is asked to assert is minutes to a readable result, and it is the one the harness cannot honestly produce. On the fake scene every step is instant. Worse, the number that looks like it measures this today does not: score-platform.json's gate_waits record the interval between the driver noticing a pause and the policy deciding, which is a property of the driver's poll loop, not of a person.
items.rootCause: audit/scoring/platform_report.py:150-176 computes gate waits from the driver's own 'advanced' and 'gate.decided' events. The same gate on two runs of the same subject reads 73 seconds and 4 seconds — AZN's PLAN gate against AZN #2's — because the poll interval changed between runs, not because anything about the gate did.

items.title: The targets, stated before the work: what result lets the operator say each issue is fixed
items.problem: Without thresholds fixed in advance, a re-measurement becomes an exercise in finding the dimension that improved. The audit's own numbers make that easy: 779 checkable figures with zero contradictions and 259 of 259 citations verified are available to quote on any day, and they were already true on the day six of six judges refused to act on the document.
items.rootCause: No target document exists. The audit set thresholds for its four criteria (§1's table) but none for the two issues the operator has now named, and §8 item 16 hands the call on "ready" back to the operator without a number attached to it.
evidence: Audit §1 table: the four criteria and their thresholds
Audit §8 item 16: "The call on 'ready'. The numbers in §3 and §4 are mine; the judgement is yours."
Counted from reads.json: 0 of 54 comparison-dimension votes went to the platform (51 console, 3 equal)
Audit §4.1: "Would you act on it? no — 6 of 6" for the platform; reads.json agreement shows azn2 also 'no' 3 of 3, so 9 of 9 across three documents
Audit §4.3 use case 8: of eighteen judge-readings of the three focus questions, the platform answered none "yes"
Audit §3.1: three of six runs reached an approved, rendered report
items.recommendation:
Pre-register these, in a document committed before the first paid run.

ISSUE 2 is fixed when, on the pre-registered round: (a) at least 4 of 6 blind comparisons name the platform on "better answers the brief" — against 0 of 9 today; (b) no platform document draws "would you act on it: no" from more than one of its three judges, and at least 2 of 3 say "with reservations" or better — against 0 of 9 today; (c) every focus question is answered "yes" or "partly" by 3 of 3 judges, with at least one outright "yes" per document — against zero "yes" in eighteen readings; (d) an investment view is stated and argued by 3 of 3 on every platform document; (e) the platform is named better on verifiability in at least 4 of 6 comparisons — against 0 of 9; and (f) nothing technical regresses: zero contradicted numerals by the audit's matcher, 100% citation verification, every blocking metric at its threshold, and every run at or under £10.

ISSUE 1 is fixed when: (a) the journey harness is green on every row of the dead-end inventory, with zero states offering no forward control; (b) zero UUIDs and zero unledgered raw identifiers in visible page text across every page the journey visits; (c) zero pages instruct the reader to run a command; (d) 3 of 3 live runs in the re-measurement window reach an approved, rendered report with no terminal use and no rescue — against 3 of 6 in September; and (e) the operator walks §4.4's six by-hand checks and testing-by-hand's scorecard with no [B] row failing.

Stated unflatteringly: (a) on ISSUE 2 is a bar the platform currently misses by the maximum possible margin, and "at least split" — 3 of 6 — would be a defensible weaker target the operator can choose instead, but it should be chosen now rather than after the result is known.
items.tests: Not a test. The guard is the commit order: the target document's hash must predate the first run's commission timestamp, and the protocol says so.
items.acceptance: A committed document naming every threshold above, with its September value beside it, dated before the first paid run of the round.

Either write the allow-list of permitted identifiers as part of the journey harness, or restate ISSUE-1 (b) as the two counts that are already unambiguous today: zero UUIDs in visible text, and zero pages whose visible text names a CLI command.

items.title: Promote the numeral matcher to a run-time metric — advisory, and only with a mutation corpus that proves it can fail
items.problem: §8 item 15 names the matcher against the filing as one of two scorers that earned a permanent place. It is the only check in the whole apparatus that does not trust the platform's record of itself: it re-reads the archived companyfacts bytes and classifies every numeral in the rendered text. But it was calibrated to zero on the platform's own reports — every contradiction it raised there was closed by a rule — so promoted as-is it is a metric that has never been shown capable of failing on the corpus it would gate.
items.rootCause: audit/scoring/text_accuracy.py:23-40 wires the three pieces: build/load truth from the archived artefact (facts.py:228-272), extract numerals (numerals.py), classify and summarise (match.py:247-262). All of it is deterministic Python over bytes already in the local store — the right side of the one rule. What is missing is negative evidence: §2 records that every apparent contradiction on a platform report was a misread, and §6 records fifteen tightenings, each of which cost recall by definition.

Audit §9: "Its precision was calibrated, its recall was not measured"

items.recommendation: Move numerals/facts/match into src/aer/eval/ as a run-time metric — call it filing_agreement — and register it as advisory, not blocking, until its recall is measured. Cost per report at run time is effectively nil: no model call, no network, one artefact read from the local store plus a regex pass over ~14,000 words, which is why this is the cheapest permanent instrument available. Ship it with a mutation corpus: take a committed report, perturb k figures by a scale factor, a digit transposition and a period shift, and assert the metric catches at least m of them. That corpus is the recall measurement §9 says was never made, and it is what makes promotion honest rather than decorative. Back-testing is possible on all five September reports without the database, because report.md, truth.json and score-text.json are committed for every one of them.

items.title: Do not promote the run-to-run variance comparison to a run-time metric — and take the one it gives free
items.problem: audit/scoring/variance.py is the instrument behind the audit's strongest reliability claim, and it is the one scorer that must not become a per-report metric: it needs two runs of the same subject, and one of its inputs is a model-proposed assumption the operator confirmed, so a "failure" can be the design working.
items.rootCause: §3.1 established that 837 calculation rows compared with 18 keys differing, and every difference traced to three inputs — the day's closing price, one extra day in the beta regression, and the exit multiple the operator confirmed at 14× rather than 15×, which moved value per share from $512.50 to $485.29. That is ADR 0046 behaving correctly, and a metric that flagged it would be measuring the operator.

Then take the free result: the recommended ISSUE-2 design already commissions MSFT twice, so run variance over that pair and report it, which re-proves the reliability claim at no extra cost. Pre-register what a pass looks like — every differing key traceable to the price of the day, the beta regression's extra observations, or an assumption the operator confirmed — so a genuine arithmetic divergence is distinguishable from the design.
